summary: Compile per-subsystem engineering packs from existing sources only — zero invention

mechanisms.title: UI block identity — consumer product IS the UI block; it carries, it does not think
mechanisms.body: The §1.0 locked schema states: "The operator asks through the UI; the request runs on the Host (Claude CLI — agent runtime + model in one)". The UI sits between Human and Host in the first-layer pipeline Human → UI → Host → Daemon{Orchestration → System of Process} → SoR / External World. The second-order draft fixes the boundary rule on the Host neighbor stub: "the request runs here; the UI carries intent down + results up — it does NOT think (sec.1.0)". Authority + Tenancy "gates every access" — drawn as the dashed wrap around the entire runtime diagram, UI included. The manifest states the page identity criterion verbatim: "consumer-product = UI block identity stated".

mechanisms.title: MECE re-cut — Channels · Ask · Receive, Standing surfaces as a Receive sub-case, render-only annotations
mechanisms.body: The UI second order is a MECE re-cut "per founder-accepted DeepSeek review" (WORKING DRAFT 2026-06-11, not locked). Engine parts are three: Channels (transport in/out the operator already uses), Ask (utterance → intent read → journey fan-out), and Receive (how Native talks back). Standing surfaces are folded into Receive as the SUB-CASE "scheduled / proactive Receive": Daily Pulse (H.3), capability map (H.1), proactive capability surfacing (H.2), weekly retro (H.4) — "all land as scheduled / proactive deliveries". Trust moments are folded INSIDE Ask (ask-side) and Receive (receive-side) rather than standing alone. Need-surfaces (5 JTBDs × 4 personas — how surfaces are discovered/justified) and Adaptation (skill modes SM1–SM3 + personalization E.1–E.4) are demoted to RENDER-ONLY annotations that "must NOT leak into the engine as a part". The footer records the full fold: "Standing surfaces folded into Receive, Trust moments folded into Ask/Receive, Need-surfaces + Adaptation demoted to render-only annotations".

mechanisms.title: Ask — 5 intent types, journey fan-out, multi-turn carry, ask-side trust gating
mechanisms.body: Every utterance resolves to one of 5 intent types (Task / Query / Directive / Feedback / New Idea, B.2) and fans out to journeys C.1–C.5 (B.5). Multi-turn carry holds: recent intent, named entities, active charter, deferred follow-ups, open questions (B.3). Trust moments live INSIDE this flow: confirm-back below confidence threshold (B.4 high/medium/low/very-low ladder) and the ask-before-acting gate (F.1/F.5: irreversible → multi-step confirm; high-risk → one-tap confirm; new authority → grant once/always/no; first-time channel → preview before send). On the Host contract: "Intent passes down only after Ask-side trust gating (confirm-back / ask-before-acting), with Authority + Tenancy gating every access".

mechanisms.title: Receive — 6 modalities, 3 landing times, modality routed by ask shape, receive-side trust
mechanisms.body: Receive defines how Native talks back: 6 response modalities (M1 text reply, M2 Slack ping, M3 email, M4 summary card, M5 approval-ask card, M6 scheduled reminder — D.1), 3 landing times (sync / scheduled / async — D.2), modality routing by ask shape (D.4). Standing surfaces are a CASE OF Receive: Daily Pulse (H.3, four fixed blocks Yesterday/Open/Suggested/Signal), capability map (H.1 by-job/by-domain/by-stage), proactive capability surfacing (H.2), weekly retro (H.4). Receive-side trust moments fold in as the M5 approval-ask card, reversibility tags (F.2 reversible / reversible-with-effort / not-reversible), and on-demand audit replay (F.3 "show me what you did and why"). The A+T gate glyph is rendered on the result edge at the M5 approval-card moment — "rendered on edges where approval moments surface, never as a pipeline box".

mechanisms.title: Channels — Day-1 transport in, 3-rule channel order out
mechanisms.body: Channels are the "transport in/out the operator already uses". Inbound Day-1 modalities: text chat, Slack mention, email forward, scheduled prompt; voice and screenshot are marked Future (B.1). Outbound channel is picked by the 3-rule order — explicit channel stated > standing preference > default-to-origin — with a one-step escalation override when time-sensitive AND the default channel is async (D.3). Edge labels carry the same contract: "delivery · M1–M6 · 3 landing times" and "channel: explicit > standing > origin (D.3)".

mechanisms.title: Operator-visible states strip — error · empty · onboarding · notification
mechanisms.body: Error: misclassified-intent confirm-back with yes/no/clarify (G.1, one focused question max); failed action stated plainly in operator words with 3 recovery options, no stack traces or codes (G.2); operator overrides "stop" / "undo" / "different approach" (G.3); wrong-answer retry loop where two consecutive misses escalate to operator walkthrough (G.4); every correction visibly acknowledged and carried forward, never silent (G.5). Empty is the "I don't know what to ask for" surface: structured capability map by job / domain / stage — live today / available-unused / unlocks-on-grant (H.1); Daily Pulse before the operator opens the surface (H.3); proactive surfacing on adjacent-ask, repeated-manual (3x), and dormant-fit triggers — soft offers that never block and decay after two declines (H.2); re-engagement when dormant via "no new asks in 5 days" (I.6). Onboarding: first session ~10 min ends with one piece of actual work done (I.1), then staged Day 1 → Week 1 → Month 1 (OHS 3–6 band) → Day 90+ (I.2–I.5), with drop-off triggers + recovery moves (I.6: pulse unopened 3 days → shrink to 3 lines). Notification: scheduled deliveries at a stated moment and async completion reports with receipt confirmed up front (D.2); escalation override promotes the channel one step (chat → Slack DM → SMS-tier) and notes why (D.3); cadence/quiet-hours bounds come from the charter (E.2); output discipline defaults to least-noise. All states "land via Receive (M1–M6 deliveries)" per the E7 edge.

mechanisms.title: Neighbor contracts — Human in/out, Host down/up
mechanisms.body: Human → UI (in): operator utterance — freeform intent resolving to one of 5 intent types, arriving over Day-1 input modalities, with multi-turn context carried across turns. UI → Human (out): delivery in one of 6 modalities at one of 3 landing times, channel selected by 3-rule order with time-sensitive escalation override; carries the operator-visible states (error, empty/capability, onboarding, notification). UI → Host (down): per the locked schema "the operator asks through the UI; the request runs on the Host (Claude CLI — agent runtime + model in one)"; intent passes down only after Ask-side trust gating. Host → UI (up): "Results back up from the platform run — Orchestration translates and finds the process, System of Process runs it gathering context from System of Record + External World and writing output back to the System of Record; the UI delivers those results to the Human via Receive".

mechanisms.title: Cross-cuts beside the doc spine — Authority/Tenancy, Observability, Resilience
mechanisms.body: The page sits on the doc spine Needs → Consumer Product → Platform Product → Implementation, with cross-cutting entries beside the spine — "they gate or instrument every layer rather than living inside one". Authority/Tenancy: "Authority + Tenancy gates every access" (the §1.0 wrap), with engine-side gate detail at D.6 (also the authority-default reference for skill modes in A.9). Observability: §7 owns per-pillar quality metrics, drift signals, operator satisfaction signals (incl. skill-mode misdetection rate per A.9), audit + replay surfaces — instruments cross-cuttingly per the §1.1 layer diagram. Resilience: §4.10 contract gives operator-visible failure behavior for hardstops HS-1..HS-8 — "the operator never debugs the system; the system tells the operator what happened, what's safe next, what needs operator decision".

mechanisms.title: UI in the pillar × block matrix — B1 PRIMARY home
mechanisms.body: In the pillar × block grid, UI is PRIMARY for B1 "Ask in my own words": "Freeform utterance enters here; parsed intent + schema preview echo back on the same surface within one turn (B1 interaction strip)". UI is SUPPORTING for B2 ("'Show me the context used' returns a ranked artifact list; narrowing ('drop the Q1 deck') re-ranks from the same surface"), B3 ("B3a brainstorm moments + B3c PRESENT (decision-ready output) face the operator; refinement returns to B3a, not a fresh B1 ask"), and B5 ("Replay/explain questions ('what did we decide last week?') and standing prefs written directly from the surface"). The B4 UI cell is empty — "no stated involvement in the doc". The B1 traversal diagram shows UI as a strong-blue PRIMARY box receiving "freeform utterance" and echoing "parsed intent + schema preview" back from the Host.

mechanisms.title: B1 Intent canon behind the Ask surface — capture, verify, clarify-never-guess
mechanisms.body: Canon B1 defines the NEW primitive Intent { high_level, specifics, expected_output_schema, post_check } — "capture user intent (high-level 'what user wants') and specifics (detailed sub-tasks); pre-LLM declare expected output schema, post-LLM check actual, measure". UX flow: operator utterance arrives via H-Sutra; classifier extracts high_level (verbatim founder voice); on missing specifics a clarification_needed predicate trips and "flows back to operator before continuing". Multi-intent composition (one utterance carries multiple intents) is "not v1; founder may slice manually". The §11.0 worked-sample User viewpoint renders the same contract on the surface: "plain words in — no command, no schema, no form"; Native confirms with a confidence number; "if unclear (conf < 0.6) → ONE clarifying question; never guess".

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — boxed decision / approval-ask surface (dir/D20 + dir/D23)
mechanisms.body: Production D20: "When two or more high-priority items compete for the same resources, the system presents the tension (what competes, why each matters, stakes) as an interactive boxed question and blocks on the operator's choice — it never resolves the conflict autonomously"; enforcement is behavioral-HARD via AskUserQuestion plus CLAUDE.md's 'Highlight decisions visually' presentation contract (ASCII-boxed, impossible to miss). Production D23: on detected conflict with any existing principle, "the system surfaces the conflict naming the specific principle violated and HOLDS — no execution path proceeds until explicit founder approval; absence of approval means no-op, never best-effort". Both dossiers name the existing Native landing machinery: "Native already has the machinery (ADR-009 approval-gate primitive, ESCALATED lifecycle state, M5 approval-ask card)". The D20 redo recipe targets this UI surface directly: "transition to ESCALATED and emit an approval-ask card framed as present-tension-with-options (port the what-competes/why-each-matters/stakes structure verbatim)"; resolution "requires an explicit operator selection event before either item proceeds".

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — Table Shape output contract at the render/presentation stage (cap/115)
mechanisms.body: Production ships the Table Shape contract as fleet policy (sutra-defaults.json .output_discipline.table_shape, v2.26.0); operative rule verbatim: "Every task list (review/backlog/roadmap/recommendations) carries Impact + Effort columns. Severity/Priority/Score alone insufficient — they rank but do not frame." It defines minimum_header '| # | Area/Task | Impact (who/what changes) | Effort (time, files) |', applies_to task_lists_3_or_more_rows, and applies_to_relayed: subagent_and_codex_output_reshape_before_presenting. Enforcement is convention_only — CSM status 'shipping (policy-visible)' is terminal for this cap. The dossier's redo recipe places it on this block: "Port the rule text and minimum_header string verbatim as a Native output-policy node attached to the render/presentation stage", explicitly including the applies_to_relayed clause as "the differentiating half of the contract and the part with no Native trace".

mechanisms.title: Host block identity — Claude CLI, agent runtime + model in one (fused)
mechanisms.body: The §1.0 locked schema: "the request runs on the Host (Claude CLI — agent runtime + model in one)"; the diagram's Host rect carries only the labels "Host" / "Claude CLI" with NO separate LLM box. The second-order draft draws agent runtime and model as one fused unit — "single block, no internal edge to a separate LLM box — the doc explicitly collapses them". The Host then carries the request downward into the Daemon on the edge labeled "runs", where Orchestration translates it and selects the process. A return edge comes back up from System of Process: when a process runs, it invokes a host LLM selected per workflow — "so the Host slot is entered from below as well as above". Everything sits inside the Authority + Tenancy gate wrap and stands on the Compute base layer.

mechanisms.title: Internal parts — agent runtime · model · per-workflow host-LLM slot
mechanisms.body: Agent runtime: "the agent-execution half of Claude CLI"; "the doc gives no further sub-decomposition (no tool loop, session, or context-window detail in the cited ranges)". Model: "the LLM, fused into the same block as the runtime — 'agent runtime + model in one'". Per-workflow host-LLM slot: "the Host position is a selectable slot, not hardwired to Claude" — ADR-005 host-llm-host-selection (ratified), with the draft quoting the master §12.1 ADR-table label "Per-workflow host LLM selection (claude · codex · deepseek)" and §4.0's canon-link citing ADR-005 as part of the shipped daemon runtime at sutra/marketplace/native/.

mechanisms.title: Neighbor contracts — UI in, Daemon out (runs + lifecycle), SoP host-LLM return, A+T wrap, Compute base
mechanisms.body: UI → Host (in): operator request — "The operator asks through the UI; the request runs on the Host" (unlabeled §1.0 arrow). Host → Daemon (out): request handoff into the always-on Daemon where Orchestration "translates the request and finds the relevant process to run"; the draft NOTES the §1.0 edge is labeled "runs" (Host runs the Daemon), not "forwards" — "the doc fuses request-flow and run-relationship on one edge". Host → Daemon (lifecycle): "Started by Sutra plugin at session boot OR by explicit sutra native start. Re-exec across plugin updates without state loss"; lifecycle START → RUNNING → STOP → RESTART (state restored from user-kit + decision-provenance log). System of Process → Host (in): host-LLM invocation per workflow (ADR-005) — "the running process calls back into a host LLM chosen per workflow". Authority + Tenancy gates every access (cross-cutting wrap, Host included); Compute carries the runs-on relationship — "base layer, no data payload".

mechanisms.title: ADR-005 — per-workflow host-LLM selection (claude --bare vs codex exec)
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST require WorkflowStep.host ∈ {claude, codex} whenever action='invoke_host_llm'". host='claude' invokes claude --bare — recursion-safe (no plugin sync, no CLAUDE.md auto-load, no hooks; skips keychain reads so unauthenticated for connector calls); default for steps that must execute in the founder's session via the effector split (ADR-004). host='codex' invokes codex exec — read-only sandbox; default for analysis, review, planning steps producing JSON/text without state change. Per-step timeout_ms flows into host activity args; host-class default 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s for codex (per Wave 1 evidence on DayFlow). Context for the lock: recursive Claude without --bare "re-loads the same plugin governance pipeline that produced the Workflow, doubling token cost AND potentially recursing forever". Tradeoff locked to these two hosts in v1.x; the LLMSubstrate adapter for OpenAI/Gemini swap is deferred to backlog OS-21; OS-20 (per-invocation MCP context passing for claude --bare) also deferred. Consequence rows: "Workflow author chooses the trust profile per step explicitly (no hidden default)"; "Steps that need BOTH authenticated mutation AND sandboxed analysis must split into two steps".

mechanisms.title: ADR-004 — registry-and-effector split: the Host session is the effector
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST be the registry + audit layer; the founder's interactive host-LLM session MUST be the effector that performs declared mutations". Native owns Workflow JSON, Trigger predicates, Execution rows, EngineEvent audit, DecisionProvenance, Tenant isolation; Claude (founder session) owns filesystem writes, git operations, network calls — "driven by Workflow steps but executed in the authenticated session". The split is recorded on every Execution via the agent_identity chain. Consequences: daemon stays unauthenticated and recursion-safe (no credential exfil surface); founder retains ASK-gate visibility on every mutation; audit records intent BEFORE the Claude effector runs (replayable); autonomous fire-and-forget workflows are blocked at v1.0 (deferred to v1.3 per OS-1/OS-2). RUN canon states the same boundary: "The host-LLM session is the effector boundary (§5.1) — file/git/network mutations declared in the Workflow happen there, not in Native. Native persists EngineEvents; the host writes the actual side effects."

mechanisms.title: ADR-021 — Sutra plugin is HOST-RESIDENT (Host gap #4 CLOSED)
mechanisms.body: Decision (Accepted 2026-06-12, founder-delegated, parity T5): "The Sutra plugin is HOST-RESIDENT. It is the governance layer the Host (Claude CLI) loads per-session" — hooks = Host lifecycle interceptors (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit); skills = Host-invokable bundles (slash-command surface); per-turn blocks = Host-emitted discipline (header, routing, depth, blueprint, build-layer, trace); sutra-defaults.json = policy payload the Host-resident layer carries. Daemon-side analogs (workflow registry, EngineEvents, schedules) live in Orchestration / System of Process; upstream governance CONTENT the plugin transports is Authority+Tenancy material — "the plugin is its transport, not its home"; no new block is added and §1.0 stays locked. Consequences: parity ledger rows for plugin-implemented concepts anchor to Host (+ projection to their content's altitude); future plugin capabilities declare Host-residency by default; "the 17 shipped-but-unwired hooks (parity T1 finding) are Host-resident dormant mechanisms; wire-or-retire review is an ops follow-up, not a placement question". Master §4.12.4 records the same: status ACCEPTED 2026-06-12, Host block open gap #4 CLOSED; dual-lane — deepseek reviewed this run, codex retro queued (auth).

mechanisms.title: Daemon lifecycle via the Host-resident plugin (§4.0)
mechanisms.body: Native runs as a per-operator local daemon the operator doesn't see; home directory ~/.sutra-native/ contains user-kit (charters, domains, triggers, workflows), decision-provenance.jsonl, native.log. Process model: "Single background daemon process per operator. Started by Sutra plugin at session boot OR by explicit sutra native start. Re-exec across plugin updates without state loss" — operator-visible: "No (managed by plugin)". Lifecycle: START (plugin launch / cron / cold boot) → RUNNING (workflow dispatches + hook firings + cadence ticks + audit writes) → STOP (plugin shutdown / explicit stop) → RESTART (state restored from user-kit + decision-provenance log). Canon link: full daemon runtime ships at sutra/marketplace/native/bin/sutra-native + sutra/marketplace/native/src/, with ADR-005 host-LLM selection, ADR-013 telemetry-sink-fsync-jsonl, ADR-017 cron-daemon-cadence-tick. The Host draft cautions: "the lifecycle edge is drawn from the Host only on the partial support of §1.0's 'runs' label", with the plugin now placed Host-resident per ADR-021.

mechanisms.title: WorkflowStep.host canon contract (step.md + run.md + B11 prompt composition)
mechanisms.body: Canon WorkflowStep: host: 'claude' | 'codex' | null — "required IFF action === 'invoke_host_llm' (ADR-005)"; host=null for non-host-llm actions, rejected otherwise; prompt_template likewise required IFF invoke_host_llm; timeout_ms is a per-step override that "flows into host activity args". Step dispatch: "invoke_host_llm spawns host subprocess"; step_started events carry payload {step_index, host, timeout_ms}. RUN surface invariants: RUN-I4 — "WorkflowStep.action='invoke_host_llm' requires host ∈ {claude, codex} AND prompt_template non-null"; RUN-I7 — per-step timeout_ms defaults to host-class default when null: 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s expected for complex codex tasks per §6.7. The RUN C4 diagram shows the dispatch chain: LiteExecutor.executeWorkflow → step action invoke_host_llm → host-LLM dispatch (claude --bare | codex exec) → on_host_llm_result → GATE/step_completed → AUDIT JSONL. Canon gap stated in run.md: §3.1 declares NativeEngine.on_host_llm_result(execId, stepIdx, r) as the resumption callback after the host-LLM returns, "but the exact wire is open per §8 OS-1". Upstream of the dispatch, canon B11 PromptBuilder fires when "Workflow step S where action='invoke_host_llm' is about to fire" and "composes prompt from all 5 sources (Domain, Charter, Artifacts, Inputs, Intent specifics)".

mechanisms.title: ADR-015 — vendored H-Sutra producer; UserPromptSubmit intake on the Host
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST vendor its own H-Sutra producer (per-turn-h-sutra.sh + classify.sh) inside the native@sutra plugin; MUST NOT depend on core@sutra at runtime" — required because a T4 user installing Native without the core plugin would otherwise hit a runtime missing-dependency error (founder direction D49). Both producers must emit the identical 9-cell + 3-tag row shape per the shared charter; when core@sutra is also installed, each plugin writes its own log path and CLAUDE.md routes which is canonical per session. Append is fail-CLOSED at row level; missing rows never block downstream Edit/Write/Bash. mechanisms.title: Block contract — translate the request, find the process (§1.0 locked schema)
mechanisms.body: §1.0 states the runtime at a glance: "the operator asks through the UI; the request runs on the Host (Claude CLI — agent runtime + model in one); inside the always-on Daemon, Orchestration translates the request and finds the relevant process to run; the System of Process runs it (this is the runtime)". The §1.0 diagram edge Host→Daemon is labeled "runs"; the Orchestration→System-of-Process edge is labeled "task = process". "Authority + Tenancy gates every access" — the dashed wrap encloses the whole stack including the Daemon's Orchestration box; no Orchestration-specific gate behavior is detailed in the cited ranges. §1.0 also assigns second-level detail (context-build · verify · connectors) to System of Process, not Orchestration.

mechanisms.title: Boundary contracts — Host in, Host confirm-back out, SoP out, Authority gates
mechanisms.body: Host (in): operator request dispatched into the Daemon, arriving as freeform utterance via Day-1 modalities — text chat, Slack mention, email forward, scheduled prompt (voice + screenshot future, per §2.F.B.1). Host (out): confirm-back / ASK BACK to the operator when confidence is below threshold (§2.F.B.4–B.5) — clarification question, operator answers, flow resumes; the B1 interaction strip also shows a schema preview returned before execution ({ metrics:[], sources:[], format:one-pager }). System of Process (out): the selected process on the "task = process" edge — carried content per B1 acceptance is parsed intent_type + structured sub-intents (typed intent) against a pre-declared output schema; System of Process then runs it as THE runtime. Authority + Tenancy (gates): "Authority + Tenancy gates every access". The draft notes §1.0 shows no upward return edge Orchestration→Host for the confirm-back (gap 6).

mechanisms.title: Internal parts — 8-part intent machinery (second-order, fully wired)
mechanisms.body: The second-order draft wires eight internal parts. Trigger intake: utterance · cadence (cron) · event per §4.1 Trigger primitive; the daemon fires scheduled triggers (§4.0), so clocked input enters the same translate/find-the-process path. Request translator: first half of the stated job ("Orchestration translates the request"), the group frame holding the intent machinery. Intent Layer: per B1 Ring 2 contract — parses freeform utterance into typed intent + sub-intents, pre-declared output schema shown before the LLM call, post-LLM output validated and rejected if non-conforming, plus show-by-example and trusted-names shortcut. Intent classifier: every utterance resolves to one of five types — Task, Query, Directive, Feedback, New Idea — each distinguished by a 'tell' (§2.F.B.2). Multi-turn context carry: five things persist across turns/sessions — recent intents (last 3-5 asks), named entities, active charter, deferred follow-ups, open questions (§2.F.B.3). Confidence gate: four bands — high → proceed; medium → yes/no confirm; low → "I read this as a task — is that right?"; very low → "act, answer, or remember?" (§2.F.B.4). Intent→journey fan-out: TASK→§C.1 · QUERY→§C.2 · DIRECTIVE→§C.3 · FEEDBACK→§C.4 · NEW IDEA→§C.5 · UNKNOWN→ASK BACK (§2.F.B.5). Process finder: second half of the stated job — "finds the relevant process to run"; matching mechanism not named in the cited master ranges (draft gap 2).

mechanisms.title: B1 Intent primitive — typed intent with pre/post gate (canon)
mechanisms.body: Canon B1 defines the NEW primitive Intent { high_level, specifics, expected_output_schema, post_check } — "the testing-framework analog at the intent layer". Flow: classifier extracts high_level verbatim; decomposer (B2) extracts specifics; the Intent primitive is instantiated with both plus a Workflow-author-declared expected_output_schema; on Workflow completion post_check evaluates output against the intent schema — pass → workflow_completed, fail → routes via canon on_failure per §6.5. Acceptance: schema is captured at Workflow registration (W-hash content-addressed); specifics missing trips a clarification_needed predicate that flows back to the operator before continuing. Edge cases: no expected_output_schema → Workflow rejected at registration; multi-intent utterance is not v1 (canon-silent gap per F2). B1 pairs with B7: B7 is the per-LLM-step gate, B1 the per-INTENT gate framing the whole Workflow.

mechanisms.title: ROUTE surface — classify utterance → matched Workflow OR pattern proposal
mechanisms.body: ROUTE is the body of NativeEngine.handleHSutraEvent: the H-Sutra event bus (§5.3) tails the per-turn JSONL log and HSutraConnector forwards each row; Router.route(evt) returns a RoutingDecision synchronously (routeAsync is the latent path per §8 OS-8). Invariants: ROUTE-I1 — every HSutraEvent produces exactly one routing_decision EngineEvent (matched or unmatched); ROUTE-I2 — routing_decision.execution_id is null (routing happens outside any Execution); ROUTE-I3 — a matched target_workflow_id MUST resolve in the registry; ROUTE-I4 — no match makes the utterance a candidate for the pattern detector (k counter increment), no Workflow fires; ROUTE-I5 (2026-06-12 PROTO-006 lesson-port amendment) — routing precedes every operator-originated action, with the operative ladder verbatim: "Process exists? → follow it. Cannot follow? → resolve without skipping. Still blocked? → STOP, ask human. Never write 'TBD.'" Falsification test: any trace showing a Workflow fired without a preceding routing_decision, or a blocked step resolved by silent skip, proves ROUTE-I5 violated.

mechanisms.title: routing_decision event (#1 of 26) — schema, emitter, consumers, fail-closed
mechanisms.body: Emitted unconditionally for every HSutraEvent that reaches the Router — including no-match outcomes — so every founder turn has a routing audit trail. CloudEvents 1.0 form with payload { execution_id: null, matched_workflow_id (W-hash or null), predicate_id, score, agent_identity, ts_ms }. Router is the exclusive emitter. Consumers: AUDIT always persists per ADR-013 3-channel durability; LiteExecutor consumes a matched decision and prepares the Execution (causal predecessor of precondition_check #10 and workflow_started #2); the EMERGE pattern detector counts no-match events for k≥4 emergence detection. When matched_workflow_id is null the event is terminal for that HSutraEvent. Fail-closed on emission failure: if the append fails across all 3 durability channels, HS-4 fires — governance hooks BLOCK; no fail-open semantic.

mechanisms.title: Process finding via TriggerSpec registry (canon mechanism behind the 'process finder')
mechanisms.body: Canon TriggerSpec declares WHEN a Workflow fires: pattern ∈ {preprocessor, observer, gate, fan_out, negotiation}, a typed predicate (match-all / match-any / cron — NEVER free prose, ADR-012 PNC parser, HARD mint-time reject), a target_workflow_id that MUST resolve in the user-kit registry (runtime HARD reject — no firing — if the target is later deprecated), and an optional cadence object per ADR-017. "The Router uses TriggerSpecs to map operator utterances (and cadence ticks) to target Workflows." Active utterance-driven path: Router consults Triggers for every HSutraEvent; on match it emits routing_decision and dispatches NativeEngine.run(target_workflow_id, ctx). Match miss: Router emits routing_decision with no matched_workflow_id, or routes to the pattern-proposal flow per ADR-010 if k≥4 unmatched utterances accumulate. An INDEX.jsonl at ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/triggers/ enumerates {id, pattern, target_workflow_id, has_cadence, ts_minted_ms} for Router fast-path lookup.

mechanisms.title: ADR-010 — no-match path: organic emergence propose-approve at k≥4
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST require explicit founder approval via approve P-<id> utterance to register any pattern-detected Workflow; the detector MUST propose only at k≥4 utterance matches." The pattern detector reads the H-Sutra JSONL (ADR-013) and tracks per-pattern hit count + sample utterances; at k≥4 with no registered workflow matching, it emits pattern_proposed (event 12) with draft Workflow JSON + samples. Founder approve P-<id> → proposal_approved (event 13) → register Workflow; reject P-<id> <reason> → proposal_rejected (event 14). Threshold rationale: k=2 too noisy, k=3 still ambiguous, k=4 is the smallest k where a pattern is consistently a real workflow; auto-register was rejected (no oversight — can mint workflows from typos), k≥5 rejected (founder loses the "Native noticed!" moment). D45 established organic emergence as a v1.2 goal that must remain founder-gated.

mechanisms.title: §11.0 B1 worked sample — the 4-viewpoint engineering shape for intent intake
mechanisms.body: Master §11.0 ships the L3 drill-down for S1 Intent (B1) as the WORKED SAMPLE every other subsystem reuses. User viewpoint: "plain words in — no command, no schema, no form"; Native confirms ("Got it — TASK, routing to Action. Confidence 0.81") and "if unclear … ONE clarifying question; never guess". System viewpoint: raw_text → [Intake Capture] → .tmp/native-utterance.txt → [Classifier] (single LLM call) → { intent, confidence, routed_to, clarify } → intake_log.jsonl (fsync, append-only, ADR-013); conf >= 0.6 gates a clarify loop vs EngineEvent intake.classified routed to B2/B3. AI viewpoint: prompt = system(role + HOW dims) + utterance + trusted-names; intent ∈ {ask, task, direction, feedback} + sub-intents + confidence; HOW dimension selected ("decompose" vs "direct" vs "consult"); EVAL GATE: golden set (50) >= 90% correct-route as the agentic accept bar; low-conf → clarify ("test-before-conclude: never assert a guess"). Everything viewpoint stitches: runs inside PLATFORM (daemon), routes to B2/B3 by intent_type, gated by B5 GOVERN (authority + HS), every turn logged to OBSERVABILITY.

mechanisms.title: D17 — capture ALL founder statements; multi-intent decomposition is the missing B1 mechanism
mechanisms.body: Doctrine: "Capture ALL founder statements in rapid succession… Check message queue before responding"; enforcement row: agent must enumerate all statements before responding — count(actions) must cover count(statements). The hard substrate that ships is capture-prompt.sh (plugin L0, UserPromptSubmit): losslessly appends every founder prompt as {ts, session_id, prompt} to holding/state/prompts/YYYY-MM.jsonl with kill-switches and never-block semantics, so a missed statement is permanently recoverable. Redo recipe names the Orchestration-side mechanism production never built: a multi-intent decomposition step in the B1 intent layer that splits one turn into N statements, emits one queued work item per statement, and runs a coverage check (work items >= statements) before the turn closes. Gap the source states: B1 intent canon explicitly defers multi-intent composition ('not v1; founder may slice manually'); no capture-all-parallel-statements contract or statements-vs-actions coverage check exists in the Native runtime.

mechanisms.title: cap/116 PROTO-006 — process-discipline routing ladder (shipped, now ported as ROUTE-I5)
mechanisms.body: Production ships PROTO-006 as constitutional protocol + fleet schema: trigger = agent receives a task OR cannot complete a required process step; check = "Process exists? -> follow it. Cannot follow? -> resolve without skipping. Still blocked? -> STOP, ask human. Never write 'TBD.'"; fleet schema rule = "When in doubt about whether to ship: route via dispatcher — read SUTRA-CONFIG/CLAUDE.md, classify input (TYPE/ROUTE), emit Depth + BLUEPRINT, then act. No silent skips." Only the named founder override phrases ('skip the process' / 'just do it' / 'skip depth assessment') suspend it. The dossier's redo recipe — wire it into the workflow engine's pre-action decision points rather than leaving it memory-only, and resolve the HARD-vs-SOFT label inconsistency — landed in canon on 2026-06-12 as the ROUTE-I5 amendment: every HSutraEvent passes through ROUTE before RUN or EMERGE, and no bypass handler exists. Enforcement today is convention-only / policy-visible terminal (CSM cap-116).

mechanisms.title: Block contract — runs the process; THE runtime (§1.0 + §4 header)
mechanisms.body: §1.0: "the System of Process runs it (this is the runtime), gathering context from the System of Record + the External World and writing output back to the System of Record"; "Second-level detail (context-build · verify · connectors) lives inside System of Process — see §4". §4 header defines purpose: "The substrate that scopes, deploys, and supervises a workforce of agents. CoS (and future products) ride on it." Owns: Charters (fixed/flex) · Agents (on-demand materialization) · Method routing per task tier · Authority gates · State envelope between pillars · Audit substrate (DecisionProvenance). Depends on §5 Connector layer (any out-of-process tool call) and §7 Observability (instruments platform health). Does NOT own: operator surface, pillar UX, pricing, channels. "Native is the engine room. Operators don't see Native directly — they see CoS."

mechanisms.title: Boundary contracts — Orchestration, SoR, External World, Host, Authority, Observability
mechanisms.body: From the second-order draft contracts table: Orchestration (in) — "task = process"; at runtime granularity this arrives as a Workflow dispatch on Trigger fire (operator utterance, cadence cron, or event). System of Record (bidirectional) — "context + output": reads operator context (context_envelope my_own; user-kit markdown Charter/Domain/Workflow specs as authoritative state per ADR-008); writes back artifacts + ExecutionResults + b5_writes + triple-channel audit (DecisionProvenance JSONL gate-log/provenance/artifact). External World (bidirectional) — "context + effects" via the Connector layer; outbound external-effect calls (send / write / delete / pay) each pass the Authority gate; inbound responses return into envelope outbound[].inbound_responses; connector half-failures drop the workflow into DEGRADED. Host (out) — LLM calls at Step granularity; the Step primitive (§4.1) is the doc's only LLM-call site, which implies System of Process is the Host caller; an explicit only-SoP-calls-Host rule is not yet stated anywhere in the doc (open gap). Authority + Tenancy (gates) — Authority gate fires at every external-effect call; escalations captured as Approval primitive; cross-tenant default-deny with explicit delegates_to edge required (HS-3 + ADR-006). Observability (out) — accuracy KPI (% of outputs passing first-time test vs needing retry); daemon health surfaced only via Daily Pulse health row; audit replay surfaces.

mechanisms.title: Runtime daemon substrate (§4.0)
mechanisms.body: Native runs as a per-operator local background daemon the operator doesn't see; it manages workforce deployment, audit-log writes, hook firing, and cadence scheduling silently. Home directory ~/.sutra-native/ — user-kit (charters, domains, triggers, workflows), decision-provenance.jsonl, native.log. Process model: single background daemon per operator, started by the Sutra plugin at session boot or by explicit sutra native start; re-exec across plugin updates without state loss. Lifecycle: START → RUNNING (handles workflow dispatches + hook firings + cadence ticks + audit writes) → STOP → RESTART (state restored from user-kit + decision-provenance log); operator-visible only via the Daily Pulse health row. State persistence: 3-channel audit (DecisionProvenance JSONL + stderr beacon + tmp fallback per HS-4 + ADR-013); user-kit markdown files are authoritative state per ADR-008. Boundary: per-Tenant isolated (HS-3 + ADR-006); cross-tenant calls require explicit delegates_to edge; default-deny. Shipped runtime lives under sutra/marketplace/native/ (CLI launcher bin/sutra-native + src/), path corrected 2026-05-13 per §10.10 P1 #5.

mechanisms.title: 10 typed primitives — and what is NOT a primitive (§4.1)
mechanisms.body: Native runtime uses 10 typed primitives per canon at sutra/os/native/primitives/: Domain, Charter, Workflow, Step, Trigger, ExecutionResult, EngineEvent (26-event catalog), Tenant, Approval, DecisionProvenance. Step is "where work happens": pre-declared expected output + LLM call OR deterministic action + post-call check (per P2 pre/post-LLM-validation). Trigger is what fires a Workflow — operator utterance, cadence (cron), or event; trigger spec lives in the Workflow file. ExecutionResult is what a Workflow produced — typed output artifact, status, audit row references; operator-readable summary, system-readable for next iteration (P1 artifact-first). Explicitly NOT primitives anymore: "Agent" (composed from Workflow + Step + Charter scope + Authority gate), "Method routing" (per-Step config + HOW Engine in §3), "Audit substrate" (replaced by DecisionProvenance + 3-channel ADR-013).

mechanisms.title: Workflow primitive — content-addressed, typed-gated unit of operator work (canon)
mechanisms.body: Workflow encodes the WHAT (steps), the WHEN (triggers via TriggerSpec), the GATING (preconditions / postconditions / requires_approval / failure_policy), and the OWNERSHIP (custody_owner / tenant boundaries). id = sha256(canonical_form(workflow)) — content-addressed W-hash; any field change yields a new Workflow id (immutable; new mint required). Invariants: I-5 step_graph reachable from step[0] via failure_policy edges (T1-T6 terminal checks — no orphan steps, no unreachable terminal, no infinite loops without explicit continue); F-13 reuse_tag=true requires non-null return_contract (mint-time rejection); F-7 modifies_sutra=true requires reflexive_check Constraint cleared or HS-1 fires; ADR-012 — preconditions/postconditions MUST parse as typed PNC predicates, free prose rejected at mint-time. Lifecycle: Mint → Dormant → Triggered → Running → Terminal (per I-14 exactly one of {workflow_completed, workflow_failed, approval_requested}); rollback events are RECOVERY transitions after workflow_failed, NOT terminal; Decommission via deprecated=true prevents new Executions. Registry rows at ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/workflows/<id>.json with INDEX.jsonl.

mechanisms.title: WorkflowStep primitive — smallest dispatchable unit; the only LLM-call site (canon)
mechanisms.body: Each Step is either a skill_ref (named pre-registered Skill) XOR an action (registered action kinds: invoke_host_llm, emit_event, etc.) — never both (I-3; F-4 + F-5 forbid both-null and both-non-null; mint-time HARD reject). host ∈ {claude, codex} and prompt_template are required IFF action === 'invoke_host_llm' (ADR-005). on_failure defaults to the parent Workflow.failure_policy (same enum-of-5 per ADR-011); every inputs[i]/outputs[i] carries schema_ref + authoritative_status per ADR-008. Approval gate: requires_approval=true pauses BEFORE dispatching the action — emits approval_requested (#15), persists a ledger row at user-kit/pending-approvals/E-<id>.json (I-15), Execution state → awaiting_approval; resume via approve E-<id> utterance → NativeEngine.resumeApproved(execId). Dispatch kinds: invoke_host_llm spawns a host subprocess; emit_event writes an EngineEvent row; skill_ref resolves to a sub-Workflow via SkillEngine.resolve. Step terminal-events (step_completed, step_paused) are NOT in I-14's terminal set — I-14 binds the parent Execution, not individual Steps.

mechanisms.title: ExecutionResult — the runtime instantiation IS the audit trail (canon)
mechanisms.body: ExecutionResult is a content-addressed E-<hash> row capturing the trigger that fired it, the running/terminal state, the append-only EngineEvent log, per-step results, parent/sibling lineage (parent_exec_id, sibling_group for fan_out groups), failure reason, agent_identity chain (ADR-015), tenant_context (ADR-006), and a partial flag for failure_policy='continue' semantics; "every founder-meaningful change to the system flows through some ExecutionResult; ExecutionResult IS the audit trail". State enum is the 6-set {running, success, failed, awaiting_approval, paused, declared_gap}. Invariants: I-4 — failure_reason === null IFF state ∈ {success, declared_gap} (HARD-checked at terminal_check); I-14 — exactly one terminal EngineEvent from {workflow_completed, workflow_failed, approval_requested}; I-15 — awaiting_approval requires a persisted pending-approvals ledger row; I-7 — ≥1 DecisionProvenance per consequential decision; I-8 — tenant_context.tenant_id non-null when crossing tenants, cross-tenant without delegates_to is an HS-3 violation; logs[] is append-only, replay-safe. Failure routing per Step.on_failure: abort → workflow_failed; escalate → workflow_escalated (#24); rollback → workflow_failed then recovery events #19-#23; pause → state paused (non-terminal); continue → partial=true and advance.

mechanisms.title: RUN surface — fire matched Workflow, dispatch steps, host-LLM at the effector boundary (canon)
mechanisms.body: RUN: "Fire a matched Workflow → dispatch each WorkflowStep → for action='invoke_host_llm' steps, hand the prompt to the configured host (claude --bare or codex exec) → persist a typed Execution log." Two operator paths: via ROUTE matched-workflow (NativeEngine.run(workflowId, ctx) from handleHSutraEvent, §3.1) and via CLI (sutra-native run <workflow-id>, §3.3). Invariants RUN-I1..I7: exactly one workflow_started per fired Workflow; every step dispatch emits exactly one step_started and one of step_completed/step_paused/step-failed routing; terminal Execution emits exactly one of workflow_completed/workflow_failed/rollback_complete/rollback_partial; invoke_host_llm requires host ∈ {claude, codex} and non-null prompt_template; failure_policy ∈ 5-set; per-step timeout_ms defaults to host-class default — 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s expected for complex codex tasks per §6.7. "RUN executes within the Native daemon. The host-LLM session is the effector boundary (§5.1) — file/git/network mutations declared in the Workflow happen there, not in Native. Native persists EngineEvents; the host writes the actual side effects." Canon gap: NativeEngine.on_host_llm_result(execId, stepIdx, r) is the resumption callback but the exact wire is open per §8 OS-1.

mechanisms.title: ADR-004 + ADR-005 — registry-and-effector split; host selection two-knob lock
mechanisms.body: ADR-004 decision: "Native engine MUST be the registry + audit layer; the founder's interactive host-LLM session MUST be the effector that performs declared mutations." Native owns Workflow JSON, Trigger predicates, Execution rows, EngineEvent audit, DecisionProvenance, Tenant isolation; Claude (founder session) owns filesystem writes, git operations, network calls; the split is recorded on every Execution via the agent_identity chain (ADR-015); v1.3 may add per-Workflow sandbox config but the split remains the default. Rationale: host: claude --bare skips keychain reads (recursion-safe but unauthenticated) and host: codex defaults to a read-only sandbox. ADR-005 decision: "Native engine MUST require WorkflowStep.host ∈ {claude, codex} whenever action='invoke_host_llm'" — claude --bare is recursion-safe (no plugin sync, no CLAUDE.md auto-load, no hooks), default for effector-split execution; codex exec is read-only sandbox, default for analysis/review/planning steps; the two hosts have orthogonal trust profiles (bare = no recursion, codex = no mutation). The lock is v1.x; LLMSubstrate adapter for OpenAI/Gemini swap is deferred to backlog OS-21.

mechanisms.title: ADR-011 + ADR-012 — closed 5-set failure policy; typed PNC predicates over prose
mechanisms.body: ADR-011: "Native engine MUST define step.on_failure as exactly one of {rollback, escalate, pause, abort, continue} — closed 5-set, no extension without ADR." rollback compensates steps in reverse (workflow_rollback_started → _complete or _partial); escalate emits workflow_escalated and routes to the founder channel; pause emits step_paused, persists a queue entry, resumes on signal; abort emits workflow_failed immediately; continue logs the failure, advances to step[i+1], sets partial=true. Workflow.failure_policy is the default; step.on_failure overrides per-step; each policy has a typed event family (events 4, 7, 19-24) — no free-form failure log; a sixth policy requires a new ADR + new event types + parser + executor branch (extension cost is deliberate). ADR-012: "Native engine MUST parse Workflow.preconditions, Workflow.postconditions, Workflow.failure_policy, and step.on_failure as typed machine-checkable predicates — not free prose"; parser surface is match-all / match-any / cron / typed comparison against execution context; evaluated at runtime via precondition_check (#10) and postcondition_check (#11); commitment_broken (#25) references a Charter obligation id resolvable in the registry (I-16); F-10 forbids English-only routing/gating positions (HARD reject at primitive-mint). Evidence: the 13-case run report showed prose PNC declared at mint but never eval-checked at runtime — silent guarantee failure.

mechanisms.title: ADR-009 — approval gate as Workflow-level primitive (typed pause, ledger, utterance resume)
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST add requires_approval: bool at both Workflow and WorkflowStep levels, and emit/handle the typed event triplet approval_requested → approval_granted | approval_denied." A step with requires_approval=true reaching the executor emits approval_requested; the Execution transitions to awaiting_approval; a ledger row persists at user-kit/pending-approvals/E-<id>.json (I-15). Founder utterance approve E-<id> → NativeEngine.resumeApproved(execId) → continue at step_index+1; reject E-<id> <reason> → approval_denied → terminal workflow_failed. Idempotent: re-fire on a resolved approval emits approval_already_handled (I-14 holds — exactly one terminal event per Execution). Context: an inline Y/N stdin gate is physically impossible (the daemon is detached from stdin, no controlling TTY); re-execute-from-scratch on approval was rejected as wasteful + non-replayable. Multi-party approval / quorum predicate is deferred (OS-15).

mechanisms.title: ADR-017 — cadence scheduling: daemon-side setInterval tick, never external cron
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST implement cadence scheduling as a daemon-side setInterval tick; MUST NOT depend on external cron / launchd." CadenceScheduler.start(intervalMs) runs inside the daemon process; on each tick, scheduled cadences whose next-fire time falls within the ±5 min window (I-12) fire TriggerEvent rows routed to the Workflow registry; each fire emits an EngineEvent + DecisionProvenance — replayable like any other Trigger. External cron was rejected for three sourced problems: macOS launchd vs Linux cron has no portable CLI surface; external cron fires are not Executions and carry no DecisionProvenance; the ±5 min tolerance (I-12) is hard to enforce across OS schedulers. A cron-string escape hatch is partially accepted as the TriggerSpec.cadence.cron field, evaluated by the daemon at tick time. Cadence examples in the charter table: per-hour Sutra-OS monitoring, per-6h team tick, daily Asawa pulse, weekly drift report, monthly comprehensive audit, quarterly stress-test.

mechanisms.title: State machine, state envelope, and how a run flows (§4.2 + §4.3 + draft narrative)
mechanisms.body: §4.2 happy path: PROPOSED (operator adds Charter) → ACTIVE (Charter live; new task T0–T3 arrives) → agent materializes scoped to that Charter → task completes → PERSISTED (artifact + audit row; output → B5.a-d) → RETIRED (operator revokes / scope expires / superseded; audit replayable forever). §4.3: pillar-to-pillar handoffs carry a typed envelope — turn_id, operator_id, charter_ref, task_tier (T0-T3), intent {type, sub_intents} from B1, context_envelope {my_own, worlds_best, peer_sutras_v2} from B2, decision_trail [{phase, factors, authority_verdict, output_ref}] from B3, outbound [{audience, channel, draft, sent_status, inbound_responses}] from B4, b5_writes {active_session_ref, provenance_row_ref, learned_pattern_updates} — Native enforces shape + authority on every handoff; the envelope must round-trip with zero data loss or HS-4 fires (§4.4). Draft run-flow narrative: steps execute in declared order (whether strictly one-at-a-time vs parallel-capable is not stated in the doc); each Step is an LLM call to the Host or a deterministic action wrapped in pre-declared-output + post-call check; hardstops HS-1..HS-8 can drop the runtime into PAUSED at any point; CSM sits alongside as the lifecycle ledger; operator feedback post-conclude feeds B5.d learned patterns.

mechanisms.title: Test-before-conclude gate (§4.5 accuracy primitive)
mechanisms.body: "Native does NOT mark a task done before testing the output. Accuracy is a per-workflow KPI. Test happens BEFORE concluding, not after." Five steps: (1) pre-declare the test per task tier — T0 atomic: grep / file-exists / contract-match; T1 multi-action: step-by-step verify + final integration check; T2 iterative: operator-visible 1-min iteration verification; T3 Charter: milestone-gate verification at goal-transition points; (2) B3 generates output (auto-execute path); (3) run the pre-declared test — determinism: same input + same Charter → same expected output shape; (4) pass → conclude + write audit row + present; fail → loop to B3 retry (max N retries per Charter), after N failures escalate to operator via Authority gate; (5) operator feedback (drop / accept / refine) becomes test signal for B5.d learned patterns; test thresholds adapt over time per workflow. Rationale verbatim: "testing AFTER means the operator sees a failure and has to ask CoS to redo. Testing BEFORE means CoS catches its own failures and retries silently." The Accuracy KPI in §7 measures % of outputs that passed first-time-test vs needed retry.

mechanisms.title: Resilience contract — hardstops HS-1..HS-8 + failure states PAUSED/ESCALATED/DEGRADED (§4.10)
mechanisms.body: The hardstop catalog defines what the system does when it cannot continue safely; every hardstop produces (a) a 1-2 sentence operator message stating WHAT happened, (b) a recommended NEXT ACTION, (c) a link to the audit row — "the operator never debugs the system". HS-1 reflexive-check refuses self-modification without reflexive_check cleared; HS-2 aborts the turn at >25% governance token overhead; HS-3 denies cross-tenant access without delegates_to; HS-4 STOPS the system when DecisionProvenance is unwritable across all 3 channels ("no silent unaudited execution"); HS-5 pauses cutover into HITL when rollback itself fails; HS-6 suspends the session on 3+ governance-hook failures in one turn; HS-7 blocks shipments when the codex queue exceeds 20 items or 7-day staleness; HS-8 auto-rolls-back on canary regression. MECHANISM-PENDING callout (2026-05-13): HS-4..HS-8 are doctrine, mechanism pending — live detectors/executors do NOT yet exist in the shipped runtime; HS-1..HS-3 have at least partial enforcement via existing plugin hooks. §4.10.2 failure states extend the §4.2 happy path: PAUSED (hardstop fired or Charter Authority needs operator decision; exit via operator decide → ACTIVE or RETIRED), ESCALATED (B3 retry budget exhausted per §4.5, or Authority gate triggers ESCALATE class per ADR-018 contract 1; operator gets a B3a THINK 3-angle brainstorm + recommended angle), DEGRADED (connector half-fail / partial side-effect; exit via idempotent retry or manual log-write reconciliation).

mechanisms.title: 7d Lifecycle Orchestrator — 8-phase lifecycle as first-class Execution state (canon)
mechanisms.body: Sutra's 8-phase task lifecycle (OBJECTIVE → OBSERVE → SHAPE → PLAN → EXECUTE → MEASURE → OPERATIONALIZE → LEARN per D30a) becomes Native's first-class Execution-state phases: ExecutionResult gains a lifecycle_phase enum (per Q16 default 2026-05-09, founder-ratified — field-level extension, no new §2 primitive). Phase consumers: OBJECTIVE consumes B1 Intent; OBSERVE consumes 7a context-structuring; SHAPE consumes B2 Decomposition; PLAN consumes B11 PromptBuilder; EXECUTE runs the Workflow steps (host-LLM dispatch per §5.1); MEASURE evaluates B7 pre/post predicates; OPERATIONALIZE registers the Workflow for cadence-fire (§6.4 / ADR-017), gated v1 by per-cycle founder approval per Q13; LEARN closes the loop. Once operationalized, the Workflow re-fires per TriggerSpec on its cadence; each fire gets a fresh ExecutionResult sharing parent lifecycle lineage via parent_exec_id. Phase failure routes through canon on_failure machinery per §6.5 — the lifecycle does NOT auto-skip phases (no canon authorization for skip). Fully autonomous auto-run is out of scope v1 (Q13 defers to v2+ once a ≥30d clean-cadence trust signal lands); two lifecycles racing to operationalize the same Workflow are handled by the B13 ConcurrencyCoordinator.

mechanisms.title: B13 Multi-Runtime Concurrency — ConcurrencyCoordinator with file-based locks (canon)
mechanisms.body: Two simultaneous runtime processes interact safely via a NEW ConcurrencyCoordinator (§12.17 row B13): file-based locks per Q33 default (matches the existing JSONL fsync pattern; portable + observable) on Artifact.id and ExecutionResult.id, with the lock table visible across processes. Flow: Runtime A acquires locks on the artifacts/executions it touches; Runtime B observes the lock and waits OR exits depending on policy (canon-silent on the wait-vs-exit default — runtime implementation choice); on release, B proceeds with a fresh read. Lock-file write failure (filesystem error) fires HS-4 per canon §6.9.4, fail-closed. Out of scope v1: DB-style serializable transactions (Q33 rejects for v1), optimistic concurrency with retry (v2 upgrade if perf signal lands), deadlock detection (explicitly v2 per §12.17), cross-process replay (§8 OS-3 deferred).

mechanisms.title: ADR-014 — depth-router as Native's own Workflow (context-build dogfood)
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST implement the depth-router as the W-load-native-context Workflow — fires codex exec, emits a structured load-plan JSON via return_contract, persists an Execution row." The Workflow uses host='codex' (read-only sandbox per ADR-005) — analysis only, no mutation; inputs are turn context, depth signal, task class slug; outputs are a load-plan JSON {include: [paths], exclude: [paths], rationale} schema-validated by return_contract; Execution row + EngineEvent audit apply the same as any Workflow. Rejected alternatives: a bash script reading docs (no audit row, no return_contract validation, no Execution lineage) and inline LLM logic in-session (not replayable; deterministic load-matrix not provable). The pattern is the canonical example of "Native runs Native" — reuse_tag=true makes it discoverable as a Skill via SkillEngine.resolve.

mechanisms.title: ADR-022 — full-loop six mechanisms (system-of-work science) — runtime mechanisms #2-#4
mechanisms.body: Accepted 2026-06-12 (founder direction in-session: "fold the gap map into canon"). Five disciplines converge on: a work system = contracted units + provably-safe composition + an append-only record from which the system can be rebuilt (replay) or rediscovered (mining); the full loop is design → execute → record → compare → redesign, with a formal result guarding each edge — "Native today runs design → execute → record". Runtime-side mechanisms adopted: #2 Registration-at-birth — a new workflow declares contract + reads/writes (→ where-used index) + version (effort S); #3 Workflow authoring engine — observe situation → Cynefin classify (fixed-sequence vs declarative form) → draft typed Workflow with per-step contracts → machine soundness check → ADR-010 propose/approve (effort L); #4 Comparator + admission — reference limits per workflow + escalation, and an open-Execution WIP cap that gates new runs (effort M). Sequence 1→2→3→4→5; the loop closes at #5 (the miner); #6 industry packs run parallel anytime after 3 with the engine staying domain-free.

mechanisms.title: proto/002 — never-substitute barrier: orchestrator waits for ALL sibling Executions
mechanisms.body: Production rule verbatim (fired as a SOFT PostToolUse warning when parallel-agent signals exist): "Do NOT write synthesis/output until ALL agents complete. Read ALL agent outputs before proceeding. Do NOT substitute your own work for pending agent work." Origin incidents: Maze HOD 2026-04-04 (orchestrator wrote report over 3 running agents and missed 6 bugs) and Dharmik SEO 2026-04-07 (compiled before 4 agents returned). Redo recipe: Native should NOT port the /tmp-mtime heuristic — the daemon owns Execution rows with terminal states, so reimplement as a first-class barrier invariant: an orchestrating Execution may not transition to synthesis/terminal while any sibling_group member Execution is non-terminal; on violation, block or queue rather than warn. Gap the source states: Native has sibling_group lineage and B13 artifact locks but no stated barrier/join rule. Keep a SOFT advisory analog only for host-LLM sessions outside daemon control.

mechanisms.title: dir/D24 — Bernstein-conditions wave dispatch as a scheduler invariant on B13
mechanisms.body: Production artifact: PARALLELIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md — a formal independence test using Bernstein conditions (write_set(A) ∩ read_set(B) = ∅ etc., with shared external state like deploy targets counted in both sets), conflict-graph construction over enumerated read/write sets, and a Bulk Synchronous Parallel wave-dispatch model — born from the 2026-04-05 incident where 15 agents across 4 planned waves collapsed after wave 1. Behavior contract: before dispatching concurrent agents, tasks are partitioned into waves whose members pairwise satisfy Bernstein conditions over declared read/write sets; conflicting tasks queue for the next wave/cycle instead of running concurrently. Redo recipe: port the formal core verbatim and express in Native as a scheduler invariant layered onto B13 runtime concurrency — each workflow step declares read/write sets, the engine derives the conflict graph, and overlap means queue-don't-run; infra/self-mutation work queues downstream actions for the next cycle rather than mutating mid-wave (composes with Native's 7e mid-exec mutation rules). Gap the source states: Native covers execution-time parallelism (B13) and mid-exec mutation (7e) but not the concurrent-evolution-while-in-use discipline nor the Bernstein/BSP formal test.

mechanisms.title: dir/D20 — competing-priorities trigger feeding ESCALATED + approval-ask
mechanisms.body: Doctrine: "When high-priority items compete, do NOT pick autonomously. Present the tension — what competes, why each matters, what's at stake — and let the founder decide. Applies at every level: company, initiative, task." Enforcement row is HARD — "agent must ask, not decide" — with mechanism AskUserQuestion plus the boxed-decision presentation contract. Redo recipe (the source's own runtime mapping): Native already has the machinery (ADR-009 approval-gate primitive, ESCALATED lifecycle state, M5 approval-ask card) — add the missing trigger class: when the scheduler/planner detects 2+ queued items with conflicting resource claims at comparable priority, transition to ESCALATED and emit an approval-ask card framed as present-tension-with-options (port the what-competes/why-each-matters/stakes structure verbatim); resolution requires an explicit operator selection event before either item proceeds. Gap the source states: Native has escalation machinery but lacks the competing-priorities trigger itself; maps to requirement N32.

mechanisms.title: engine/coverage — process-coverage system reimplemented as daemon EngineEvent emission
mechanisms.body: Production ships a complete live process-coverage system: COVERAGE-ENGINE.md depth-indexed expected checklists (D1=4, D2=7, D3=14, D4=19, D5=24 method IDs), the machine-readable os/method-registry.jsonl (26 methods × id/category/min_depth/required_at/phase/conditional), deterministic PostToolUse auto-fire mapping (path-glob→method, command-substring→method, per-turn dedupe), a Stop-time gap gate (expected = enabled_methods INTERSECT required_at[depth], SOFT), and a coverage-fires-per-commit adoption metric. Redo recipe: port method-registry.jsonl verbatim as a Native SoR table; "reimplement the writer as EngineEvent emission in the daemon: port auto-coverage.sh's case tables as declarative data … with the daemon owning per-turn dedupe, so coverage rows become Execution-linked events instead of grep-appended JSONL"; reimplement gate and report as queries over those events, keeping SOFT-first with codified HARD triggers (per-method fire rate >85% stable 90 days → individually HARD-gate; <60% session coverage → block checkpoint). Gap the source states: Native names the Coverage Engine only in the §11.3 engines listing and lacks all five shipped layers; per-turn hooks enforce marker presence but measure nothing about session-level process completion.

mechanisms.title: dir/D31 + dir/D32 — per-tenant capability switches and hot-reload enablement at fire time
mechanisms.body: D31 behavior contract: a client runtime cannot skip a Sutra-prescribed method — any skip attempt exits 2 with feedback-path instructions; methods activate only via Sutra-pushed config flips (default false); coverage gaps at the task's depth are surfaced at session end. D31 redo: "Model in Native as per-tenant capability switches (default false) in tenant config owned by the platform, an execution logger with no runtime-skip parameter … and a Stop-time coverage gate computing enabled ∩ required-at-depth"; keep the three-phase SOFT→HARD→telemetry hardening schedule. D32 behavior contract: a hook fires iff its registry row exists AND enabled_hooks[name]: true; newly declared hooks are inert by default; adding a registry row reaches running sessions on the very next tool call without restart; every enablement flip is a git-auditable config commit. D32 redo: "In Native this maps to the Trigger registry plus per-tenant enablement read at fire time rather than load time"; carry content-hash tamper detection as a v2 item. Gaps the sources state: both mechanisms have only one-line clauses in §10.5 — the per-client switches, removed skip path, and hot-reload contract are unspecified in the runtime spec (D31 maps to N36).

mechanisms.title: proto/023 — per-instance runtime config: one sourceable knob surface for daemon + hooks
mechanisms.body: Production ships one shell-sourceable file per instance at $HOME/.sutra/config.env holding every kill-switch, threshold, and opt-in, plus a bin/sutra-config CLI (get/set/list/init/path) that preserves inline comments and validates UPPERCASE_ALNUM_UNDERSCORE keys; the contract is ADDITIVE — pre-existing env-var overrides keep working. Default keys include kill-switches (SUTRA_RTK_ENABLED, SUTRA_CODEX_DIRECTIVE_ENABLED, …), thresholds (SUTRA_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS=600000, SUTRA_DEPTH_DEFAULT=5, SUTRA_BUILD_LAYER_DEFAULT=L0), observability (SUTRA_TELEMETRY=off), and tier (SUTRA_TIER=governance). Redo recipe: "Native's typed declarative config (B10/P10) covers schema but not the operational knob surface — reimplement as a Native-owned per-instance runtime config: one sourceable/parseable file the daemon AND host-side hooks both read, holding the kill-switch registry, thresholds, and tier"; redesign the CLI as a sutra-native subcommand; "mandate (and lint) that every Native hardstop/hook declares its kill-switch key in this registry — production never closed the adoption loop (1 of ~75 hooks sources it)". Gap the source states: no sutra-config, config.env, or kill-switch-registry concept is traced in Native.
