mechanisms.title: Four-horizon substrate B5.a–d — parallel time horizons, not a graduation pipeline
mechanisms.body: The four stores B5.a–d are parallel time horizons, not a graduation pipeline — the PERSISTED step writes output to B5.a/b/c/d simultaneously. B5.a (minutes–hours) is what's right-now in flight and backs N22 session-continuity with handoff of open threads. B5.b (hours–days) holds multi-task state for the 5 in-flight tasks across N companies, survives session restart, and backs N24; its engineering hard-problem (token budget allocation + multi-thread state machine) is deferred to Phase 2 design. B5.c (days–forever) accumulates the append-only DecisionProvenance rows forever and backs N#8, with acceptance: 100% of decisions carry a DecisionProvenance row and replay of any task end-to-end in ≤30s for a single-day window. B5.d (months–forever) distills learned patterns at k=4 emergence and backs N#5; operator standing prefs land here and future B2 reads them. B2 reads from this block at intake (ranked context retrieval) and B1 reads it for shorthand interpretation on future turns. The §1.0 diagram splits SoR contents as "own | external".

mechanisms.title: Per-turn 5-artifact audit trail (§7.2)
mechanisms.body: Every Native turn produces 5 stored artifacts: 1. intent record (B1), 2. context manifest with ranked artifact list + what was dropped (B2), 3. decision provenance with phases + factors + authority verdict + output (B3), 4. outbound log (B4, if comms triggered), 5. substrate write (B5: active-session ref + learned-pattern updates). Operator command "replay last Paisa turn" shows all 5 artifacts chronologically; "show me what changed in B5.d this week" returns a diff of learned patterns. Observability acceptance (v1): the 5-artifact trail is emitted per turn and HS-4 fires on any missing channel. The operator can request replay for any past turn within ≤30s for a single-day window. Drift signals are tracked weekly; breach surfaces to founder via Daily Pulse. B5 drift signals named in the draft: replay latency >60s OR any cross-tenant leak.

mechanisms.title: DecisionProvenance — typed audit row primitive (ADR-007 + canon)
mechanisms.body: DecisionProvenance is Native's typed audit row for every consequential decision — Workflow-level, Step-level, Hook-level, Tenant-level, or Cutover-level; every Workflow/Execution/Hook emits ≥1 row per consequential decision (I-7). Fields per ADR-007/§2.9: id (uuid v4, unique), monotonic ts_ms, agent_identity chain (ADR-015, parent→child), policy_id + policy_version both non-empty (I-9 + I-17; empty either field is a HARD F-8 reject), scope ∈ {WORKFLOW, STEP, HOOK, TENANT, CUTOVER}, outcome ∈ {allow, deny, pause, escalate}, sanitized reason (no colons, no newlines — protects JSONL parsing), and data_refs[] each carrying authoritative_status per ADR-008. PolicyDispatcher.evaluate(scope, evidence) returns the row; UserKit.appendDecisionProvenance fsync-writes it to ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/decision-provenance.jsonl AND to the owning Tenant's audit_log_path when the decision touches a Tenant. Rows are inert immutable records — once persisted they are final, no state transitions. ADR-007's decision rationale: every consequential decision is replayable from a structured row, and policy version drift is detectable (same evidence + different policy_version → different outcome). ADR-007 rejected unstructured log append (loses policy version, fails F-8, blocks replay) and hook-scoped gate-log extension (Workflow/Step/Tenant/Cutover scopes need the same primitive uniformly).

mechanisms.title: EngineEvent — append-only typed event log with exhaustive 26-type catalog
mechanisms.body: EngineEvent is Native's append-only typed audit row — one JSONL line per event — forming the complete audit trail for Workflows, Executions, Triggers, approvals, rollbacks, pattern emergence, commitments, and tenant boundary violations. Every event carries event_type, ts_ms, execution_id?, payload, and agent_identity (per ADR-015). The 26-value event_type enum is exhaustive; new event-types require a NATIVE-ENGINE.md amendment + ADR, with mint-time reject on unknown types. Once persisted a row is immutable — no edit, no delete; replay derives full state from the log, and events MUST NOT be re-ordered by ts_ms after persistence. I-14: exactly ONE of {workflow_completed, workflow_failed, approval_requested} is emitted per Execution; recovery events are post-terminal transitions. Sinks: per-Execution log at ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/executions/E-<hash>.events.jsonl, global ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/events.jsonl (replay source), and the decision-provenance.jsonl subset. Consumers (replay, audit, telemetry-sink fan-out §5.6, H-Sutra event bus §5.3) read the events read-only.

mechanisms.title: Telemetry sink — fsync'd JSONL append (ADR-013)
mechanisms.body: Native engine MUST persist EngineEvent and DecisionProvenance as fsync'd JSONL append-only files; the H-Sutra event bus follows the same shape. One JSONL line per event/decision, UTF-8, no newline-in-field (sanitized at emit); fsync per append for durability — never lose a row on crash. Stderr beacon fallback when the primary path is unwritable, with dual fallback to /tmp (the HS-4 chain). The pattern detector (ADR-010) reads the log directly — no in-memory cache; restart-safe. Alternatives rejected: in-memory ring buffer (dies on daemon restart — codex P1.2 forced rejection) and SQLite/DB (adds dependency + schema migrations; JSONL won on append-only proof + zero-dep). Consequences: crash-safe and multi-process safe (POSIX append atomicity for short lines); no indexed query — replay is sequential scan, aggregation is downstream tooling; OTel production transport (OS-10) is the next-tier deferral, JSONL stays primary. The second-order draft labels this part "TELEMETRY SINK · ADR-013 · JSONL + fsync · no silent loss".

mechanisms.title: HS-4 — DecisionProvenance log unwritable across all 3 channels
mechanisms.body: HS-4 fires when a consequential decision must emit a DecisionProvenance row (per I-7) and the primary JSONL append fails AND the stderr beacon fallback fails AND the /tmp dual-fallback fails — all 3 channels simultaneously unavailable. Fail-mode: block all governance hooks; a stderr beacon is emitted as the surface-of-last-resort even when the audit log itself is unwritable. Per I-7 + I-9 + I-17, governance cannot proceed without a writable provenance surface — audit-trail integrity is preserved by blocking, not by writing without trace. Recovery: operator observes the beacon and restores at least one of the 3 channels before governance hooks resume. Operator-visible behavior per master §4.10.1: system STOPS and surfaces "cannot record this decision; halting until audit recovers" — no silent unaudited execution. The second-order draft and B5 acceptance add: HS-4 fires on triple-channel write failure and on any silent overwrite (version-bump-less replace per D.12 acceptance).

mechanisms.title: AUDIT surface — persistence + replay contract
mechanisms.body: Every state transition across every surface emits exactly one typed EngineEvent + (for consequential decisions) one DecisionProvenance row; AUDIT is the persistence + replay surface for those rows. AUDIT is not directly invoked — every other surface (ROUTE/RUN/GATE/EMERGE/TENANT) calls UserKit.appendDecisionProvenance(dp) or emits EngineEvent rows that AUDIT persists. Invariants AUDIT-I1..I8: ≥1 EngineEvent per transition (append-only); exactly one DecisionProvenance per consequential decision; monotonic ts_ms; sanitized reason; durability via fsync per append + 3-channel fallback + stderr beacon last-resort; fail-CLOSED on audit, never fail-open (HS-4); non-empty policy_id + policy_version; chain-shaped agent_identity per ADR-015. AUDIT persists ALL 26 EngineEvent types of §3.2. Replay per §6.1: every consequential decision is rebuildable from agent_identity + policy_id + policy_version + data_refs + outcome. Canon gaps the surface itself names: cross-process replay deferred per §8 OS-3, and an "audit_log_write_failed" event is not in §3.2 — HS-4 uses stderr beacon, not an EngineEvent.

mechanisms.title: Versioned artifact store — D.12 lifecycle integrity
mechanisms.body: Append, don't overwrite: every change adds a version (semver or date-stamped); the prior version stays accessible; no silent rewrites. Notify-on-change: when an artifact shared with audience X changes, audience X is notified by §5 Connector (Slack/email per Charter) — within 60s per acceptance. Reference-with-version: every cross-reference embeds the version it points to (e.g. paisa-Q3-onepager@v3) and resolves to that exact version even after newer versions ship. Pristine boundaries: metadata (owner, version, source-of-truth status) travels with the artifact, not in a sidecar that can desync. Audit-traceable: every artifact write produces a DecisionProvenance row linking creator-Charter + reason + diff-from-prior. Acceptance criteria (v1): 100% of Native-produced artifacts carry version + owner + Charter-ref metadata; zero silent overwrites (HS-4 fires on any write that replaces without version-bump); broken references surface to operator, never silently 404.

mechanisms.title: Personalization memory — skill modes (E.1), charter prefs (E.2), memory layers (E.3), forget rules (E.4)
mechanisms.body: Memory layers (E.3) are five layers with distinct lifespans: working memory (session, handoff if thread open); named entities (until forget or 90-day inactive + confirmed archive); trusted names (durable, change needs explicit confirmation); prior intents (rolling, older entries summarize); ratified directives (until revoked). Forget rules (E.4): one-time sensitive content, expired time-bounded charters, and anything the operator asks to forget — honored immediately and visibly confirmed. Skill modes (E.1) are a per-domain skill-mode map (SM1 novice / SM2 intermediate / SM3 expert) for how Native talks to this operator — inferred from phrasing/corrections or set explicitly; per-domain, not global; a separate mechanism from the E.2 charter. Charter & declared preferences (E.2) capture what the operator explicitly told Native about how to be served — cadence, hands-off level per ask class, communication style, channel defaults, people & relationships — durable until revoked. The operator curation surface answers "what do you remember about X?" with a structured view of entities, prior intents, standing directives, and charter entries touching X. Operator forget/correct/pin-as-durable commands enter via the UI→Host→Daemon runtime path.

mechanisms.title: Authoritative-vs-advisory state on every DataRef (ADR-008)
mechanisms.body: Native engine MUST require every DataRef to carry an explicit authoritative_status ∈ {authoritative, advisory}. Readers honor authoritative over advisory at lookup time — declarative precedence, no convention. Workflow inputs[] and outputs[] tag each entry, enforced at primitive-mint via ajv schema validation. DecisionProvenance.data_refs[] carries the same field — every audit row records which version of which surface was load-bearing (markdown vs code per row). Drift detection: weekly cadence reports the authoritative-vs-advisory diff for each known artifact pair, making drift a measurable signal instead of a surprise. Alternatives rejected: implicit "code wins" (newly-captured markdown directions must be load-bearing), implicit "markdown wins" (runtime decisions are the live contract), and single-source-of-truth collapse (both surfaces serve different audiences — founder reads markdown, daemon reads code).

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — coverage event stream as a Native SoR table (engine/coverage)
mechanisms.body: Production ships a live five-layer process-coverage system: COVERAGE-ENGINE.md depth-indexed expected checklist (D1=4, D2=7, D3=14, D4=19, D5=24 method IDs) with the coverage-log.jsonl row schema {task, depth, method, ts, evidence, skipped_reason, override} and an evidence-specificity rule ('if your evidence could describe any task, it's not evidence'); os/method-registry.jsonl encoding all 26 methods (id/category/min_depth/required_at/phase/conditional); writers log-coverage.sh (HARD-rejects any runtime skip attempt — 5th arg → exit 2, per D31 'clients execute, never skip') and auto-coverage.sh (declarative path/command → method mapping with per-turn dedupe, the dominant production writer); a Stop-time coverage-gate computing expected = enabled_methods ∩ required_at[depth]; and observability-synthesis.sh deriving coverage-fires-per-commit with RED classification when commits>0 but fires=0. The dossier's redo recipe: port os/method-registry.jsonl verbatim as a Native SoR table — it IS the contract — and reimplement the writer as EngineEvent emission in the daemon, so coverage rows become Execution-linked events instead of grep-appended JSONL. Gate and report become queries over those events, keeping SOFT-first with codified HARD triggers. The dossier's stated gap: Native names the Coverage Engine only in the §11.3 engines listing and lacks all five shipped layers.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — latency rows into the ADR-013 telemetry sink (charter/speed)
mechanisms.body: The SPEED charter ships the Iron Rule ('No Speed improvement ships without a cited time-sink baseline from this charter's data'), 8 KPI formulas with Warn/Breach thresholds (governance overhead % target <15%, breach ≥30% auto-becomes the #1 cut), the full phase taxonomy tree with an unambiguous start/end boundary-event table per phase, 8 collector invariants (I1: sum(phase_ms) within ±2% of wall), and the canonical LATENCY-LOG.jsonl row schema. The W1 collector latency-collector.sh appends one row per task (wall_ms, tool/result/thinking/subagent counts, full token usage incl. cache_read/cache_creation, partial flag), always exit 0. Operational state: the pipeline is DORMANT — dispatcher-stop.sh invokes a holding copy that no longer exists on disk and LATENCY-LOG.jsonl is frozen at 10 rows from 2026-04-20. The dossier's redo recipe: production's failure mode argues for emitting latency rows from Native's own engine events into the ADR-013 fsync-JSONL telemetry sink, so measurement cannot silently decouple from execution; port the taxonomy, formulas, invariants and row schema verbatim as the measured-universe IP. The dossier's stated gap: Native carries only scattered point latency targets (B5 replay ≤30s, pulse gen ≤60s) and misses per-task phase-resolution profiling and the <15% governance-overhead budget with a computable formula.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — fleet telemetry manifest queried over the telemetry SoR (cap/100)
mechanisms.body: Production ships fleet.sh — the 'who is running the plugin, right now' dashboard — parsing every clients/<install_id>/manifest.json in the sutra-data cache into rows {install_id, github_login, git_user_name, os_pretty, arch, tz, project_name, push_count, sutra_version, last_seen, age_days, has_identity}. Output: 5 aggregates (total installs, identified count/%, unique github logins, unique humans, total pushes) plus a per-install table sorted last_seen descending; --fresh restricts to installs seen within 7 days; an empty cache exits 1 with clone instructions. Privacy default: since plugin v2.0.0 outbound telemetry is DISABLED by default per PRIVACY.md. Ops thresholds: warn on active-installs drop >25% WoW or identified <70%; breach at 0 installs (push pipeline broken); migration trigger at fleet >50. The dossier's redo recipe: port the manifest.json interchange shape verbatim — it is the contract between client push and fleet view — and redesign the renderer as a Native query over the telemetry SoR producing the same 5 aggregates + active-within-7-days filter. The dossier's stated gap: Native has telemetry collection (ADR-013) and the tier taxonomy but the fleet-level aggregate consumption view is unspecified.

mechanisms.title: The wrap — gates every access (§1.0), drawn as border not pipeline
mechanisms.body: §1.0 draws Authority + Tenancy as a dashed wrap around the entire runtime ("AUTHORITY + TENANCY · gates every access") — a cross-cutting envelope, not an in-line stage on any single edge. Internal flow per the second-order draft: every access entering the wrap is classified by the D.6 six-dimension Authority Model, then run through the F.5 ask-vs-act cascade; any ASK outcome is realized by the approval-gate primitive (ADR-009), which surfaces the prompt up through UI carrying its F.2 reversibility tag, while the gated workflow inside System of Process holds in PAUSED or ESCALATED until the operator's decision flows back down. In parallel, the tenancy half checks every System-of-Record touch against the ADR-006 Domain field, with HS-3 default-denying cross-tenant access lacking an explicit delegates_to edge; denials surface via the hardstop UX contract (WHAT + next action + audit-row link). Operator responses ("grant always", dial up/down) feed the F.4 trust ladder, which shifts future cascade outcomes from ask toward auto over rungs 1-4. Every decision through the gate writes a DecisionProvenance row, which the F.3 replay surface reads back on demand, and the §1.5.1 guard tooling enforces the same contract at action-time as HARD/SOFT blocks.

mechanisms.title: Authority Model — six gate dimensions (D.6)
mechanisms.body: Six dimensions gate Native's auto-execute vs ask-operator decisions. By domain: Native acts in one company's domain but not another (per Charter). By tool: Native can call Slack but not bank-API without auth. By stakeholder: Native emails team but escalates board/regulator. By dollar threshold: ≤$X auto, >$X ask. By reversibility: reversible auto, irreversible ask. By confidence level: high-confidence auto, low-confidence ask. Applies cross-pillar — most heavily in B3 (action gate) and B4 (delegation through Native to humans).

mechanisms.title: Ask-vs-act decision cascade (F.1 + F.5)
mechanisms.body: Ordered 4-question cascade per action. Irreversible? → ASK multi-step confirm ("type go" two-step). High-risk (spend/send/share/commit touching people or money)? → ASK one-tap confirm ("confirm — send / edit / cancel"). New authority (no prior permission template)? → ASK "grant once / grant always / not now". First time on channel/contact? → ASK preview-before-send ("preview before I send?"). All no → ACT, report after. The cascade's ASK outcomes route to the approval-gate primitive, and GATE/ESCALATE outcomes hold the workflow in the §4.10.2 failure states.

mechanisms.title: Reversibility tags (F.2)
mechanisms.body: Every action carries a visible reversibility tag with three values. Reversible: undo window — "say undo anytime". Reversible with effort: retract/re-issue/re-pay — doable, not free. Not reversible: confirming locks it in. The tag is visible on every action and appears on every approval prompt surfaced up through UI.

mechanisms.title: Trust ladder (F.4) — autonomy earned over time
mechanisms.body: Four rungs: Rung 1 (day 0-14) ask before every external action; Rung 2 (15-45) auto-act on repeated patterns, ask on novel; Rung 3 (46-90) auto-act on routines, ask only high-risk/irreversible; Rung 4 (90+) runs standing routines and surfaces what it did. The operator can dial up/down explicitly at any rung. "Grant always" responses and dial moves feed the ladder, which shifts future cascade outcomes from ask toward auto.

mechanisms.title: Approval gate — first-class primitive (ADR-009 + canon Approval + GATE surface)
mechanisms.body: Native engine MUST add requires_approval: bool at both Workflow and WorkflowStep levels, with the typed event triplet approval_requested → approval_granted | approval_denied (ADR-009; approval is a first-class primitive, not a hook). Reaching a requires_approval=true step: LiteExecutor persists a ledger row at user-kit/pending-approvals/E-<id>.json carrying {workflow_id, step_index, ts_ms, prompt_summary} (I-15 — hardstop on absence), emits approval_requested (#15, terminal per I-14), and transitions the Execution to awaiting_approval — fail-CLOSED, pausing BEFORE dispatching the action. Founder utterance approve E-<id> → NativeEngine.resumeApproved(execId) continues at step_index+1 and emits approval_granted (#16); reject E-<id> <reason> emits approval_denied (#17) and routes per Workflow.failure_policy to workflow_failed. Idempotent re-fire on a resolved approval emits approval_already_handled (#18) carrying prior_outcome — resolution is one-shot, and ledger rows are removed on first resolution. The daemon is detached from stdin, so inline Y/N prompts are impossible — approval is utterance-driven from the founder's interactive session, and the persistent ledger row survives daemon restart. v1 ships single-founder approval (Q5 ratified 2026-05-09); multi-party quorum is deferred to v2+ per OS-15. approve P-<id> approves a proposed Workflow and routes to EMERGE (ADR-010), NOT GATE — a documented cross-surface boundary.

mechanisms.title: Tenant primitive + tenant isolation via Domain.tenant_id (ADR-006)
mechanisms.body: The Tenant primitive is Native's isolation boundary: every Domain is owned by exactly one Tenant (I-13 — required field, no nullable). Tenant fields: content-addressed id (T-hash), non-empty name, isolation_contract (filesystem + capability isolation declaration), parent_tenant_id (null for root), and an absolute audit_log_path to the Tenant's DecisionProvenance JSONL. Execution.tenant_context carries {tenant_id}, and TenantIsolation.assertCrossTenantAllowed(src, dst, op) is called unconditionally when a step touches a different tenant. Cross-tenant ops without an explicit delegates_to edge fail-closed and emit tenant_boundary_violation (#26; HS-3, I-8). ADR-006 rejected reusing Cohort (a routing/targeting primitive — a Workflow can target multiple Cohorts; a Domain belongs to exactly one Tenant) and relying solely on the D33 settings.json firewall (intent-level, not capability-enforced); D33 stays as defense-in-depth. Consequences: the tenant boundary is a typed schema field checked at primitive-mint AND execution; the audit trail records every cross-tenant attempt; migration cost — every existing Domain must be assigned a tenant_id (no default); hierarchical/nested tenancy is declared in schema but execution semantics are v1.x backlog.

mechanisms.title: HS-3 — tenant boundary cross without TenantDelegation
mechanisms.body: HS-3 fires when an Execution attempts to cross a Tenant boundary without an explicit delegates_to edge: the Execution carries tenant_context.tenant_id, a step targets a resource whose effective tenant differs, and no delegates_to edge authorizes the cross (I-8). Fail-mode: block + log + escalate — the op is blocked at TenantIsolation.assertCrossTenantAllowed, a tenant_boundary_violation event (#26) emits carrying src_tenant/dst_tenant/op, and a DecisionProvenance row is logged with policy_id='HS-3'. Fail-closed when workflow.custody_owner !== null AND tenant_context_id is undefined. Recovery requires the operator to authorize the cross via an explicit delegates_to edge. Operator-visible behavior per master §4.10.1: cross-company action DENIED, with the prompt "this action would touch <other-company>; explicit delegates_to authorization required". Master's MECHANISM-PENDING callout records that HS-3 has only partial enforcement via existing plugin hooks today.

mechanisms.title: TENANT surface — isolated audit log + ACL per company
mechanisms.body: TENANT provides each Tenant with an isolated audit log + ACL — cross-Tenant operations require explicit delegation, every Tenant's DecisionProvenance is private by default, and cross-Tenant leakage is fail-CLOSED. It is consulted on every Execution dispatch and every cross-Tenant operation; it is not a CLI surface but is enforced via TenantIsolation.assertCrossTenantAllowed, which throws on deny. Invariants: every Domain has a non-null tenant_id (TENANT-I1); every Tenant has non-empty name + absolute audit_log_path (TENANT-I2); cross-Tenant ops require TenantDelegation, else throw + #26 + HS-3 (TENANT-I3); fail-CLOSED when custody_owner !== null AND tenant_context.tenant_id undefined (TENANT-I4); each Tenant's DecisionProvenance JSONL is private absent explicit delegation (TENANT-I5); HS-3 fires block+log+escalate on any violation (TENANT-I6). Operator-visible touchpoints: Tenant mint with declared audit_log_path, `sutra-native tenant list` (§3.3), and the violation path. Upstream surfaces ROUTE/RUN/GATE/EMERGE all respect Tenant scope; downstream, AUDIT persists to the per-Tenant log and HS-3 handles violation escalation.

mechanisms.title: Hardstop UX contract + HS-1 reflexive check
mechanisms.body: Every hardstop produces (a) a 1-2 sentence operator-facing message stating WHAT happened, (b) a recommended NEXT ACTION (decide / authorize / wait / investigate), and (c) a link to the audit row for the event; the operator never has to read engineer-level stack traces — the system translates. HS-1 (reflexive check) fires when a Workflow with modifies_sutra=true attempts to write Sutra core paths (plugin hooks/skills, charter files) without the reflexive_check Constraint cleared. Fail-mode: HARD reject + Founder ASK gate — LiteExecutor rejects the step dispatch before any host-LLM call fires, a policy_decision event emits with outcome='deny' and policy_id='HS-1', a DecisionProvenance row references the F-7 violation, and the daemon surfaces the rejected step + provenance to the founder via the approval primitive (ADR-009). The Workflow does NOT auto-retry; the founder must clear the reflexive_check Constraint via explicit approval before resumption. Operator-visible per master: system REFUSES to self-modify and surfaces "this change touches Sutra's own rules — please ratify directly".

mechanisms.title: Authority-driven failure states — PAUSED / ESCALATED (§4.10.2)
mechanisms.body: PAUSED is entered when a hardstop fires (HS-N) OR Charter Authority requires an explicit operator decision (per §D.6); the operator sees "task paused at step X — decision needed" with context + recommended next action; exit path: operator decides → ACTIVE (resume) OR RETIRED (cancel). ESCALATED is entered when the B3 retry budget exhausts (per §4.5 test-before-conclude) OR the Authority gate triggers the ESCALATE class (per ADR-018 contract 1's AUTO/GATE/ESCALATE classification); the operator sees "auto-retry exhausted; your judgment needed" with a B3a THINK 3-angle brainstorm + recommended angle; exit path: operator confirms direction → ACTIVE (B3b auto-executes the chosen path) OR RETIRED. These failure states extend the §4.2 happy-path lifecycle (PROPOSED → ACTIVE → PERSISTED → RETIRED). The risk-owner map assigns R4 operator review fatigue to §D.6 Authority Model trust signal + ADR-018 contract 1, and R3 cross-tenant leakage to §4.10 HS-3 + ADR-006.

mechanisms.title: Guard tooling — §1.5.1 governance machinery (projection; primary home is governance band)
mechanisms.body: Live action-time guards enforce the authority + audit + intervention contract as HARD/SOFT blocks: when a guard fires HARD, the operator sees a boxed BLOCKED message with the rule cited + override path (typically {D_TAG}_ACK=1 {D_TAG}_ACK_REASON='<why>' <cmd> — honor-system at env-var level, audit-logged); when SOFT, the operator sees an advisory and the tool call proceeds. Tenancy-relevant rows in the §1.5.1 table: the external-client repo firewall (blocks cross-repo access from holding workspace into external client trees per D33, HARD) and god-mode (time-boxed cross-company deployment access, CEO-of-Asawa only, 2h auto-deactivate, logged to .enforcement/god-mode.log, opt-in HARD scope). The §1.5 Governance Machinery row states every decision carries a provenance row and cross-tenant is default-deny. Per the manifest, this page draws the wrap relationship to the governance band as a projection — content is not duplicated; §1.5.1 machinery's primary home is governance/ (codex MODIFY-2).

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — security charter + boundary/elevation primitives (charter/security)
mechanisms.body: Production ships SECURITY.md charter v1.0.0: a 3-threat-surface model (Surface 1 Asawa IP = confidentiality; Surface 2 fleet integrity = "one compromised push → all tenants have arbitrary code execution"; Surface 3 tenant authenticity), 8 ordered principles including fail-closed and identity boundaries ("'You're authenticated as X, I can act as X' patterns are banned"), a T0-T4 tiered access contract, and a 14-primitive inventory (8 shipped, 6 needed: signed releases, SHA-pinned submodules, god-mode MFA, update-consent, SBOM cadence, audit rollup). Shipped enforcement: enforce-boundaries.sh (PreToolUse, fail-closed role resolution, exit 2 blocks cross-submodule edits, god-mode file bypass) and god-mode.sh (password-gated 2h TTL elevation, every activate/deactivate/expiry appended to .enforcement/god-mode.log — 33 rows live). Behavior contract: any Write/Edit from a non-matching role into another submodule exits 2 with unresolvable role failing CLOSED; cross-company writes from holding succeed only inside the god-mode TTL window. The dossier's redo recipe: re-implement the tenant/role boundary as a Native hardstop keyed on ADR-006's domain field instead of bash path-matching, and god-mode as a first-class time-boxed authority-elevation primitive (TTL + append-only audit) rather than a marker file; the identity-leak defense should become enforced policy, not injected context. The dossier's stated gap: Native has the pieces piecemeal (HS-3, ADR-006, god-mode time-box) but lacks the charter's consolidating layer — the 3-surface model, the T0-T4 contract, the failure-mode→primitive map, and KR1-KR7 measurement; HLD/07 Security remains planned-only (T-G8-08 TODO).

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — competing-priorities escalation trigger (dir/D20)
mechanisms.body: D20 doctrine: "When high-priority items compete, do NOT pick autonomously. Present the tension — what competes, why each matters, what's at stake — and let the founder decide. Applies at every level: company, initiative, task." Enforcement is HARD behavioral — "agent must ask, not decide" — with AskUserQuestion as the mechanism plus the boxed-decision presentation contract; there is no dedicated hook file by design. Behavior contract: when 2+ high-priority items compete for the same resources, the system presents the tension as an interactive boxed question and blocks on the operator's choice, never resolving the conflict autonomously. The dossier's redo recipe: Native already has the machinery (ADR-009 approval-gate primitive, ESCALATED lifecycle state, M5 approval-ask card) — add the missing trigger class: when the scheduler/planner detects 2+ queued items with conflicting resource claims at comparable priority, transition to ESCALATED and emit an approval-ask card framed as present-tension-with-options, with resolution requiring an explicit operator selection event before either item proceeds. Maps to requirement N32.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — conflict-hold semantics (dir/D23)
mechanisms.body: D23 doctrine: "When a change conflicts with existing principles/directions, present the conflict and require explicit founder approval via AskUserQuestion. Without approval, the system holds. The OS challenges, the founder rules." Enforcement: "HARD — system holds until founder approves via interactive prompt. No silent overrides"; absence of approval means no-op, never best-effort. A concrete shipped instance is the operator-awareness guard: edits to charters/PERMISSIONS Tier 3/FOUNDER-DIRECTIONS/D-tagged files by a non-founder git identity are treated as REQUIRES-FOUNDER-APPROVAL with a boxed confirmation and no auto-execution. The dossier's redo recipe: implement as a conflict-detection pass over Native's direction/principle registry before any mutating action, feeding ADR-009's gate primitive in hold mode; semantics to port: fail-closed hold-by-default, the conflict statement must name the specific conflicting principle, and approval is recorded with provenance (ADR-007 schema). The pushback register belongs in doctrine text, not just gate mechanics. Maps to requirement N34.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — keys-in-env-vars boundary block (proto/004 → canon HS-9)
mechanisms.body: PROTO-004 is ACTIVE, HARD, enforced at two layers: plugin keys-in-env-vars.sh (PreToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit) scans INCOMING content for provider-shaped key regexes (sk-…, AKIA…, ghp_…, ghs_…, xoxb-…, ya29.…, AIza…, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY — OWASP/git-secrets sourced) and exit-2 BLOCKS with a JSONL audit row, exempting env-type files, privacy-scrub libs, and binaries, with PROTO004_ACK=1 + reason as the audited override and D32 default-OFF opt-in; the Asawa dispatcher Check 5 (always-on) blocks assignment-shaped secrets, with only secret-INTRODUCING edits blocked — remediation edits pass. Canon already carries the lesson-port as HS-9 (DRAFT v1, authored 2026-06-12): secrets live only in env vars/env-type files, any artifact write introducing a key-shaped string is denied at the boundary BEFORE the file is touched, and out-of-repo 0600 stores (~/.sutra-connectors/oauth/ precedent) are a second, separately-governed sanctioned pattern gated by ADR-003 (deepseek MODIFY absorbed 2026-06-12). HS-9 declares the Native kill-switch key SUTRA_HS9_KEYS_DISABLED per the B10 K4 registry mandate. Recovery: move the secret to an env var or sanctioned store and re-issue; on a historical leak, rotate the credential first — rotation is the recovery, history rewriting is not. The dossier's stated gap: Native names the hook in §4.11.A but states no key-handling invariant; §5.1 stores connector tokens in oauth JSON files with no rule explaining why that is allowed.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — role-scoped boundary confinement for the tenancy wrap (hier/l4 + hier/l5)
mechanisms.body: Production confines a company-{name} session role to its own tree via enforce-boundaries.sh: edits outside the role's repo exit 2, and role resolution fails CLOSED (exit 2) when the role cannot be determined; the D33 firewall keeps external clients as standalone repos with the plugin as the only channel. L4 blast radius ("only this company") is enforced negatively and positively: cascade-check.sh does NOT match company os/ paths (no fleet-cascade obligation), and a company-scoped role cannot write outside its own tree. L5 (application code) carries zero upward blast: edits trigger no cascade obligation, and problems discovered in code reach higher tiers only through the feedback channel (feedback-to-sutra/ then PROTO-024 gh-issues fan-in), never by directly modifying a higher level. Both dossiers' redo recipes name this subsystem as the port target: "port enforce-boundaries.sh role confinement to Native's tenancy wrap" (hier/l4) and "Port enforce-boundaries.sh's role table + fail-closed resolution into Native's tenancy wrap" (hier/l5), declaring the single-company blast radius in canon and keeping deployment-scope paths exempt from any cascade gate.

mechanisms.title: §1.0 placement — External World as runtime counterpart block (context + effects edge)
mechanisms.body: Per the §1.0 system architecture, the System of Process runs the process (this is the runtime), gathering context from the System of Record + the External World and writing output back to the System of Record; Authority + Tenancy gates every access. In the §1.0 diagram the External World box is labeled 'services · people' and its edge to System of Process carries 'context + effects' (the System of Record edge carries 'context + output'). §1.0 also states that second-level detail (context-build · verify · connectors) lives inside System of Process — see §4. ADR-021 records the locked first-layer schema as 8 blocks: UI · Host (Claude CLI) · Orchestration · System of Process · System of Record · Authority+Tenancy · Compute · External World.

mechanisms.title: Second-order internal flow — parallel counterparties, two one-way Connector lanes
mechanisms.body: The parts of the External World do not connect to each other — they are parallel counterparties, each reached over its own Connector channel. Traffic flows in two one-way lanes through the Connector transport (§5.2): on the outbound lane, System of Process output (B3's decision, B4's draft) passes the Authority gate, becomes a typed envelope with retry logic, and lands on a service endpoint (Slack, email, web, 3rd-party tool) or, through Slack/email, on a human stakeholder. On the inbound lane, a human's reply (e.g. the board chair's Slack response) is identity-verified, wrapped into a typed envelope, and routed back to B3 as the next action — so people and services only 'meet' inside System of Process, never inside the External World block. Peer Sutras have only a log-only A2A stub edge in v1 (no real transport), and browser/phone counterparts have no live edge at all. At the §1.0 altitude the whole block collapses to a single bidirectional 'context + effects' edge with System of Process, with Authority + Tenancy wrapping every crossing. The draft's System of Process neighbor stub states 'Connector lanes live here (§5.2)' — matching the manifest acceptance line 'Connector lanes live in SoP; External World owns counterparties' (codex MODIFY-4), with platform/connector.html cited for transport.

mechanisms.title: Counterparty inventory — four internal parts
mechanisms.body: The draft names four internal parts. People (operator's stakeholders): humans Native talks to on the operator's behalf — board / founder / team / client / vendor, each with audience-calibrated voice per the CX Bar overlay; the doc's worked example is a board chair receiving an audience-calibrated Slack DM and replying inbound ('got it; let's discuss Friday'). External services: service endpoints reached via Connector transport — Slack (in + out, Live), Email via Resend (out, Live — daily pulse + notifications), Web fetch/search (out, Live — feeds B2.b world's-best context), 3rd-party tools (out, pluggable via Composio with per-tool Charter scoping); §5.2 names them collectively 'THE WORLD (Slack · email · web · 3rd-pty)'. Peer Sutras: other operators' Native instances; v1 status is log-only A2A stub, no real transport; full peer-Native A2A is v2+, gated per §1.4.5 activation map. Deferred-channel counterparts: endpoints listed in the v1 inventory but not reachable yet — Browser co-work session (in + out, Charter TODO-005, deferred to v1.x, spec pending) and Phone voice + SMS humans (not planned v1, v2+ per §1.4.5 phone-connector activation gate).

mechanisms.title: Neighbor contracts — SoP edges + Authority/Tenancy wrap on every crossing
mechanisms.body: The contracts table declares four neighbor edges. System of Process (bidirectional): 'context + effects' per the §1.0 edge label — SoP gathers context FROM the External World and pushes effects INTO it; this is one of the two external edges of the runtime (the other being System of Record, which gets 'context + output'). System of Process (in): outbound sends via the Connector outbound lane (B3 → B4) — audience-calibrated draft converted to a typed envelope, Authority-gated at every send, retry logic on transient fail, DecisionProvenance row per send; permanent failures surface to operator, no silent loss. System of Process (out): inbound receives via the Connector inbound lane (B4 → B3) — identity-verified, payload converted to a typed envelope, routed to B3 as next action; inbound from unverified identity logs + drops and never enters B3; inbound responses re-enter the loop via B3 and prior comms become B2 future context. Authority + Tenancy (gates): every outbound call passes the Authority gate with default-deny on missing scope; per-tool Charter scoping enforced (e.g. 'Slack:#paisa-team only', not 'Slack:*'); B4 adds per-stakeholder + tool + $-threshold gating on who Native may talk to.

mechanisms.title: Authority + Tenancy gating of External World crossings — gate at every send, preview-before-send
mechanisms.body: The Authority+Tenancy second-order draft's gated-pair row for External World (connector sends from inside System of Process) states: Authority gate at every send — per the §1.2 boundary table, §5 Connector 'Depends on §4 Authority gate at every send'; D.6 by-tool and by-stakeholder dimensions decide which external calls auto-execute vs ask; first message to a new person/channel gets preview-before-send. D.6's six dimensions decide auto-execute vs ask-operator: by domain (per-Charter company scope), by tool (Slack yes, bank-API no without auth), by stakeholder (team auto, board/regulator escalate), by dollar threshold (≤$X auto, >$X ask), by reversibility (reversible auto, irreversible ask), by confidence level (high auto, low ask) — applying cross-pillar, heaviest in B3 action gate + B4 delegation. The matrix traversal view notes its wrap scope intentionally differs from the §1.0 drawing: §1.0 encloses the entire pipeline including External World and Compute inside the wrap; the traversal view draws External World and Compute outside it and marks the gate at the boundary-crossing edge instead.

mechanisms.title: Peer-Native A2A — B16 canon envelope (v1 stub logs intent)
mechanisms.body: B16 canon: Native instances exchange typed messages via a minimum-viable A2A envelope {src_native_id, dst_native_id, msg_type, payload, ack_id, agent_identity_chain}; ack required; v1 ships a stub that LOGS intent (per §12.17 'stub v1 logs intent') with actual delivery deferred. Envelope validation requires all 6 fields per Q35 — missing field or truncated/missing agent_identity_chain is rejected. The A2A protocol is NEW per §12.17 row B16 but is not a new §2 primitive — the protocol lives at the integration layer. Each message carries an audit + DecisionProvenance row per ADR-007; the envelope is persisted as an audit artifact via artifact_registered per P1 closed-loop. Out of scope v1: capability negotiation (Q35 v3), cross-org A2A (v3+ per P13). B16 vs B17 distinction per canon: B16 = internal Native-Native; external = Connectors (B17). Hardstop dependencies: HS-3 (tenant-boundary — A2A respects Tenant isolation) and HS-4 (audit-unwritable).

mechanisms.title: Deferred-capability activation gates for External World counterparties (§1.4.5)
mechanisms.body: Master §1.4.5 names the activation gates for the three not-yet-live counterparty channels. Full A2A transport (peer-Native agent-to-agent coordination, beyond v1 log-only stub): (1) B2.c Peer Sutras LIVE as prerequisite; (2) A2A protocol authored as canon ADR; (3) identity + auth model for cross-Native calls; (4) audit trail extends to cross-Native DecisionProvenance — on activation, B4 transport adds a peer-A2A channel and §C.4 R3 cross-tenant model + §C.4 R2 audit-log spec extend. Phone connector (voice call + SMS as Native transport — distinct from voice surface): (1) telephony provider chosen + integration tested (Twilio/Vonage candidate); (2) per-call Authority gate spec (operator approves outbound voice; inbound voice consent + recording disclosure compliant); (3) voice-data retention + PII-sanitization extends D.12; (4) cost model per minute fits §C.4 R8 budget. Browser co-work connector (operator-driven browser session as a Native-observed surface): (1) browser-driver choice ratified (Playwright/Chromium candidate per existing Sutra gstack pattern); (2) operator-consent model — operator initiates session, Native attaches read-only by default + escalates to action via Authority gate; (3) sandbox + identity isolation per HS-3 tenant-boundary; (4) audit row captures every Native-issued action against the operator's browser, with a new connector spec under sutra/marketplace/plugin/connectors/browser/.

mechanisms.title: §5 layer contract — purpose, owns, depends-on, does-not-own
mechanisms.body: §5 Connector is the transport layer: purpose is to move messages + tool calls between Native (§4) and the world outside (humans, services, peer Sutras). It owns Slack · email · web · browser · phone · 3rd-party tool integrations · inbound/outbound message handling · retry semantics. It depends on the D.6 Authority gate (at every send) and §7 Observability (for delivery health). It does NOT own what to say (B3), decision logic (B3), Charter scope (§4), or audience selection (B4 + Authority). The §1.2 layer boundary table repeats the contract — §5 owns 'Slack/email/web/browser/phone transport; 3rd-party tool integration; inbound/outbound message handling', depends on '§4 Authority gate at every send', does not own 'Decision logic; charter scope; what to say' — and records that §4 Native Platform depends on '§5 Connector for any out-of-process tool call' while §2 CoS depends on '§5 Connector transport'.

mechanisms.title: §5.2 inbound/outbound flow semantics
mechanisms.body: The §5.2 flow diagram splits Connector traffic into an outbound lane (B3 → B4) and an inbound lane (B4 → B3) on either side of §4 Native Platform. The outbound Connector applies: Authority gate, draft → typed envelope, retry logic. The inbound Connector applies: identity verify, payload → typed envelope, route to B3. Both lanes terminate at 'THE WORLD (Slack · email · web · 3rd-pty)'. The diagram caption fixes the per-message contract: every send is Authority-gated, writes a DecisionProvenance row, and retries on transient fail; every receive is identity-verified, typed-envelope wrapped, and routed to B3 as the next action.

mechanisms.title: §5.3 acceptance criteria (Connector v1)
mechanisms.body: Four acceptance criteria are stated for Connector v1. Every outbound call passes through the Authority gate; default-deny on missing scope. Inbound from unverified identity logs + drops, and doesn't enter B3. Transient failures retry; permanent failures surface to the operator (no silent drop). Per-tool scoping is enforced via Charter (e.g. 'Slack:#paisa-team only' not 'Slack:*').

mechanisms.title: B17 — every external tool is a typed Connector (canon spec)
mechanisms.body: B17 canon: every external tool (Slack, Email, web, etc.) is a typed Connector — inbound messages become Artifacts in the catalog; outbound messages emit DecisionProvenance + Artifact rows; Workflow steps are tool-aware. Per Q36 default, Connectors stay the abstraction — no new primitive class for 'external comm channels'; v1 EXTENDs existing Connectors (Slack live per memory project_connectors_slack_live; MCP servers; via plugin). The data model is Connector = {connector_id, tool_name, auth_config, inbound_handler, outbound_dispatcher}; a Workflow step declares connector_id to route via. Flow: inbound message → Connector handler emits artifact_registered (§3.2 #9) and the inbound Artifact joins the context catalog routable per 7a/B11; a step with connector_id fires outbound → Connector dispatches and emits a DecisionProvenance row per ADR-007 plus an outbound Artifact per B9. Failure handling stays canon: expired/revoked auth at dispatch routes via canon on_failure per §6.5; a Connector-emitted Artifact crossing a Tenant boundary fires HS-3 per §6.9.3. Telemetry events are artifact_registered, policy_decision, tenant_boundary_violation; metrics affected are Operator-Hours-Saved (Connectors directly displace manual cross-tool ferrying) and cross-company decision-replay success rate. The §4.11.A feature registry indexes B17 at blocks/B17-external-tools-connectors.md.

mechanisms.title: Shipped production — Connectors module (3-layer) + federation doctrine (dir/D36)
mechanisms.body: The federation half of D36 shipped: the Connectors module at plugin/connectors/ (CHARTER.md v0.1.0 ACTIVE — 3 layers: L1 Sutra policy/audit, L2 Composio auth+catalog, L3 MCP wire; ships D38 L0 fleet; ConnectorRouter.call(ctx) public API). The governing doctrine: Sutra should run on anything and federate with peer frameworks via thin connectors, never absorption — 'Where a common interface layer doesn't exist, Sutra builds the connector — never the underlying ecosystem'. Behavior contract: external-service calls route through ConnectorRouter under tier-scoped capability policy with append-only audit; runtime host LLMs are guaranteed only {claude, codex} per ADR-005, with second-opinion LLM lanes (codex, deepseek) available as governed skills; broader LLM-agnosticism is doctrine pending founder-approved phasing, not a runtime promise. Multi-LLM lanes shipped as consult/review surfaces: core:codex-sutra (OpenAI Codex), core:deepseek (DeepSeek via Anthropic-compatible API, 4 modes), and bin/deepseek-claude (separate Claude session on DeepSeek v4-pro backend). mechanisms.title: Shipped production — connector-token storage vs keys-in-env-vars HARD contract (proto/004)
mechanisms.body: PROTO-004 is ACTIVE, HARD, enforced at two layers: (1) plugin L0 hooks/keys-in-env-vars.sh, PreToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit, scans INCOMING content for provider-shaped key regexes (sk-…, AKIA…, ghp_…, ghs_…, xoxb-…, ya29.…, AIza…, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY — sourced from OWASP/git-secrets), exits 2 BLOCK with 'Put secrets in .env / env vars only' and a JSONL audit row to .enforcement/routing-misses.log; (2) the Asawa holding layer dispatcher-pretool.sh Check 5 blocks assignment-shaped (api_key|secret_key|password|token)[:=] content — the two pattern sets catch disjoint cases. Exemptions: env-type files (*.env, */secrets/*, *credentials*), privacy-scrub libs, binaries; only edits that INTRODUCE a secret are blocked (remediation edits pass); override PROTO004_ACK=1 + reason is audit-logged; default-OFF per D32 at plugin layer. The dossier's redo recipe directs Native to reconcile with §5.1 connector oauth JSON files by whitelisting ~/.sutra-connectors/oauth/** chmod-600 paths as a named legitimate secret home, mirroring the hook's *keys.json/*credentials* exemption.

mechanisms.title: HS-9 hardstop — two-pattern secret boundary reconciling §5.1 oauth token storage
mechanisms.body: HS-9 canon (DRAFT v1, authored 2026-06-12; production contract ACTIVE + HARD in Sutra, Native runtime wiring pending): secrets live only in environment variables or env-type files; any artifact write introducing a key-shaped string into a non-env file is denied at the boundary BEFORE the file is touched (exit-2 class block); remediation edits that remove secrets always pass. The scope boundary reconciles the §5.1 connector-token tension: HS-9's enforcement boundary is the repository write path; out-of-repo secret stores are NOT silently exempt — they are a second, separately-governed sanctioned pattern: untracked stores outside any repository, mode 0600, under a named location (~/.sutra-connectors/oauth/ precedent), with edits gated by the adjacent secret-file edit gate (ADR-003). Two patterns, two gates — a secret in neither pattern violates one of them (deepseek MODIFY absorbed 2026-06-12). Native kill-switch key per B10 K4 registry mandate: SUTRA_HS9_KEYS_DISABLED. STRIDE relevance: Information Disclosure primary (credential exfiltration via repository distribution), Elevation of Privilege secondary.

mechanisms.title: ADR-005 — host enum lock and the connector-authentication implication
mechanisms.body: ADR-005 (Accepted 2026-05-07) requires WorkflowStep.host ∈ {claude, codex} whenever action='invoke_host_llm'. host='claude' invokes claude --bare — recursion-safe; no plugin sync, no CLAUDE.md auto-load, no hooks; it skips keychain reads, so it is unauthenticated for connector calls. host='codex' invokes codex exec — defaults to a read-only sandbox, useful for analysis/review steps that should not mutate state. Per-step timeout_ms flows into host activity args; host-class default is 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s for codex. The tradeoff is locked to these two hosts in v1.x; the LLMSubstrate adapter for OpenAI/Gemini swap is deferred to backlog OS-21, and OS-20 (per-invocation MCP context passing for claude --bare) is also deferred. A stated consequence: steps that need BOTH authenticated mutation AND sandboxed analysis must split into two steps.

mechanisms.title: §4 runtime integration — outbound[] envelope fragment + DEGRADED half-fail state
mechanisms.body: The §4.3 state envelope carries a B4-produced fragment: outbound: [ { audience, channel, draft, sent_status, inbound_responses } ] — emitted 'if comms triggered'. The §4 Native Platform header table declares 'Depends on: §5 Connector layer (for any out-of-process tool call)'. §4.10.2 defines the DEGRADED failure state: entry condition is 'Connector half-fails (e.g., send succeeded but audit write missed); OR partial side-effect (draft created but send failed)'; the operator sees 'step partially completed — message X sent but audit row missed; reconciliation needed' with compensation options; exit is a reconciliation step (idempotent retry OR manual log-write) → ACTIVE or PAUSED. The System of Process second-order draft restates the runtime edge: external-effect calls (send / write / delete / pay) exit via connectors only after the Authority gate; inbound responses return into envelope outbound[].inbound_responses; connector half-failures drop the workflow into DEGRADED.

mechanisms.title: Compute block identity — base layer of the §1.0 runtime
mechanisms.body: §1.0 states the system as it actually runs: 'Authority + Tenancy gates every access; Host + daemon run on the Compute (host machine)'. The §1.0 SVG draws COMPUTE as a single dashed base box labeled 'COMPUTE · host machine — where the Host + daemon execute'. The second-order draft defines the host machine (execution substrate) as 'the base layer of the §1.0 runtime diagram: a single dashed box'; the doc defines it only as the machine on which Host (Claude CLI) and Daemon run, and v1 compute is per-operator and local ('Native runs as a per-operator local daemon', §4.0). The draft's footer is explicit about provenance: 'internal structure assembled from the daemon's §4.0 footprint (the doc has no Compute-section decomposition)'. The Host executes on the same machine, but the doc draws no compute-internal edge between Host and the daemon at this layer — their interaction is modeled above Compute in the §1.0 stack.

The doc states nothing beyond hosting; no interface, resource, or co-location contract is specified.' Direction is out, source anchor section-1-0-runtime. mechanisms.title: Contract to Daemon — substrate + filesystem persistence + process lifecycle + cadence ticks
mechanisms.body: The Compute→Daemon contract row in the second-order draft: 'Execution substrate + filesystem persistence (~/.sutra-native/ root, JSONL audit channels, user-kit markdown, tmp fallback) + process lifecycle (single background process per operator; cold boot is a START trigger; RESTART restores from on-disk state) + cron cadence ticks (ADR-017).' The SVG edge labels carry the same facts: 'single process per operator', 'lifecycle START → RUNNING → STOP → RESTART', '~/.sutra-native/ persistence', 'audit: JSONL · stderr · tmp'.

mechanisms.title: Per-operator filesystem state (~/.sutra-native/)
mechanisms.body: Per the second-order draft's internal-parts table: a 'Compute-resident daemon root holding user-kit (charters, domains, triggers, workflows), decision-provenance.jsonl, native.log; plus the 3-channel audit persistence (DecisionProvenance JSONL + stderr beacon + tmp fallback) and user-kit markdown as authoritative state (ADR-008). Documented under §4.0 as the daemon's footprint on the host machine; not operator-visible.' Master §4.0 states the same: home directory ~/.sutra-native/ is the per-operator daemon root, operator-visible 'No (filesystem internal)'; state persistence is '3-channel audit (DecisionProvenance JSONL + stderr beacon + tmp fallback per §4.10 HS-4 + ADR-013); user-kit markdown files for Charter / Domain / Workflow specs (per ADR-008 markdown-vs-code authoritative state)'; the operator 'can request audit replay (B5.c); never sees the JSONL directly'. During RUNNING the process facility 'reads and writes the per-operator filesystem state at ~/.sutra-native/ continuously (audit JSONL writes + user-kit markdown)' and reads it back on RESTART, 'surviving plugin re-exec without state loss'.

mechanisms.title: OS process facility — single daemon process per operator
mechanisms.body: Master §4.0 process model: 'Single background daemon process per operator. Started by Sutra plugin at session boot OR by explicit sutra native start. Re-exec across plugin updates without state loss', operator-visible 'No (managed by plugin)'. Lifecycle: 'START (plugin launch / cron / cold boot) → RUNNING (handles workflow dispatches + hook firings + cadence ticks + audit writes) → STOP (plugin shutdown / explicit stop) → RESTART (state restored from user-kit + decision-provenance log)', visible only via the Daily Pulse health row (§7). The second-order draft carries this verbatim as the OS-process-facility internal part, doc-home section-4-0-daemon. The §4.0 canon link adds: the full daemon runtime ships at sutra/marketplace/native/bin/sutra-native (CLI launcher) + sutra/marketplace/native/src/ — 'path corrected 2026-05-13 per §10.10 P1 #5: shipped runtime lives under sutra/marketplace/native/, not sutra/marketplace/plugin/'.

mechanisms.title: Cron / scheduling facility — daemon-side tick, not OS cron (ADR-017)
mechanisms.body: ADR-017 decides: 'Native engine MUST implement cadence scheduling as a daemon-side setInterval tick; MUST NOT depend on external cron / launchd.' CadenceScheduler.start(intervalMs) runs inside the daemon process; on each tick, scheduled cadences whose next-fire time falls within the ±5 min window (I-12) fire TriggerEvent rows, and each fire emits an EngineEvent + DecisionProvenance — replayable like any other Trigger. External cron/launchd was rejected as not portable across macOS/Linux, with no integration with Native's TriggerEvent lifecycle and no DecisionProvenance on fire; a cron-style escape hatch survives only as TriggerSpec.cadence.cron, evaluated by the daemon at tick time. Stated consequences: portable, auditable, ±5min verifiable inside the engine; but 'daemon must stay running for cadences to fire (start/stop discipline matters)' and per-tick CPU cost is non-zero. Master §4.0 cadence row: per-Workflow trigger spec with cadence field; the daemon fires triggers on schedule and dispatches matching Workflows; the operator 'sees the SCHEDULED OUTPUT (daily pulse, weekly synthesis, etc.); not the cron firing'. The second-order draft draws cron feeding the process facility twice: as a START trigger (alongside plugin launch and cold boot) and as recurring cadence ticks the daemon turns into Workflow dispatches per ADR-017.

mechanisms.title: On-disk durability — fsync'd JSONL append (ADR-013)
mechanisms.body: ADR-013 decides Native MUST persist EngineEvent and DecisionProvenance as fsync'd JSONL append-only files on disk: one JSONL line per event/decision, UTF-8, fsync per append — 'never lose a row on crash'. A stderr beacon fallback fires when the primary path is unwritable, with dual fallback to /tmp (the HS-4 chain). The shape was chosen against four constraints — survives daemon restart, zero new dependency, append-only audit, multi-process safe (POSIX atomic line-level appends); in-memory ring buffer and SQLite were both rejected. Stated costs: disk I/O per event (fsync is not free), and no indexed query — replay is sequential scan. This is the durability contract for everything Compute stores under ~/.sutra-native/.

mechanisms.title: Isolated replica kits via SUTRA_NATIVE_HOME (ADR-016)
mechanisms.body: ADR-016 decides: 'Native engine MUST honor SUTRA_NATIVE_HOME env var to redirect user-kit reads/writes; the Asawa replica MUST live at $HOME/.sutra-native-asawa-replica/.' Primary user-kit stays at $HOME/.sutra-native/user-kit/ (production / fleet / emergent); the replica gets distinct PID locks + distinct telemetry JSONL so 'daemons can run side-by-side without interference'. Adding the replica primitives to the primary kit was rejected for contamination risk: Workflow ID collision, mixed telemetry in the same JSONL, and no clean reset path. A reset script (bash holding/scripts/build-asawa-native-replica.sh) is idempotent — wipes + rebuilds the replica without touching primary. Stated costs: two daemons mean two memory + CPU footprints when both run, and the operator must remember to set SUTRA_NATIVE_HOME; the decision 'sets pattern for future per-tenant kit isolation as multi-tenant matures'.

mechanisms.title: Cloud-hosted compute — deferred v2+, activation-gated
mechanisms.body: The second-order draft's internal-parts table defines cloud-hosted compute as a 'managed-infra distribution channel where the operator does not run their own daemon', deferred behind activation gates: 'multi-tenant infra spec + HS-3 tenant-boundary extension to shared-host, per-tenant data-residency + key-isolation, pricing tier, cloud-managed install path. Until then, Compute = operator-local machine only.' Master §1.4.5 carries the canonical activation row: (1) multi-tenant infra spec authored + HS-3 tenant-boundary contract extends to shared-host; (2) per-tenant data-residency + key-isolation guarantees; (3) pricing tier defined (operator-economics validated per §C.4 R8); (4) onboarding flow (§6.3) gets a cloud-managed install path matrix row. The draft's internal-flow text adds: 'The deferred cloud-hosted variant (v2+) would replace the operator-local machine entirely, with no schema impact described yet.'

mechanisms.title: Authority + Tenancy wrap over Compute — boundary, no named compute-level mechanism
mechanisms.body: The second-order draft's contracts table marks Authority + Tenancy direction as 'gates': 'Cross-cutting wrap — the §1.0 diagram's dashed Authority+Tenancy boundary encloses the Compute box ("gates every access"). No compute-level enforcement mechanism is named in the doc; the only compute-adjacent tenancy fact is per-tenant isolation of the daemon (HS-3 + ADR-006, default-deny cross-tenant).' Master §4.0's Boundary row states the daemon is 'Per-Tenant isolated (per HS-3 + ADR-006); cross-tenant calls require explicit delegates_to edge; default-deny on cross-tenant data flow', visible only if HS-3 fires on an attempted boundary cross. The draft renders the wrap as a dashed boundary in its SVG ('gating renders as boundary, not a pipeline box').

mechanisms.title: Compute in the pillar × block matrix — uniform SUPPORTING substrate
mechanisms.body: The pillar × block matrix marks Compute as SUPPORTING for all five CoS pillars, with each cell stating the same pattern: the work 'runs inside the Daemon on Compute; no B<N>-specific compute fact stated' (B1 entry request, B2 retrieval, B3 execution, B4 connector transport, B5 record-keeping). In the B1 traversal SVG, Compute is drawn as the dashed substrate box ('where Host + Daemon execute · no B1-specific compute fact stated in the doc'), with the Daemon container and the Host each carrying their own runs-on edge to Compute. The matrix note records a deliberate wrap-scope difference: §1.0 encloses the entire pipeline including Compute inside the Authority+Tenancy wrap, while the traversal view draws Compute outside it and marks the gate at the boundary-crossing edge instead.
