mechanisms.title: §4 Native Platform — workforce-deployment substrate (ownership frame)
mechanisms.body: §4's 6-block frame: Purpose = 'The substrate that scopes, deploys, and supervises a workforce of agents. CoS (and future products) ride on it.' Owns = 'Charters (fixed/flex) · Agents (on-demand materialization) · Method routing per task tier · Authority gates · State envelope between pillars · Audit substrate (DecisionProvenance).' Depends on §5 Connector layer for any out-of-process tool call and §7 Observability for platform health; does NOT own operator surface, pillar UX, pricing, channels. The callout: 'Native is the engine room. Operators don't see Native directly — they see CoS (§2).' Detailed primitive definitions live in §9 D.10 (Charter Model) and D.11 (Method Selection); §4 surfaces runtime behavior + state.

mechanisms.title: §4.0 Runtime daemon — where Native lives + runs
mechanisms.body: Native runs as a per-operator local daemon; the operator doesn't see it (§A.2.2 post-onboarding zero-terminal); it 'manages workforce deployment, audit-log writes, hook firing, and cadence scheduling silently in the background'. Home directory: ~/.sutra-native/ per-operator daemon root containing user-kit (charters, domains, triggers, workflows), decision-provenance.jsonl, native.log. Process model: single background daemon process per operator, started by the Sutra plugin at session boot OR explicit 'sutra native start', re-exec across plugin updates without state loss. Lifecycle: START (plugin launch / cron / cold boot) → RUNNING (handles workflow dispatches + hook firings + cadence ticks + audit writes) → STOP → RESTART (state restored from user-kit + decision-provenance log), operator-visible only via the Daily Pulse health row (§7). State persistence is 3-channel audit (DecisionProvenance JSONL + stderr beacon + tmp fallback per §4.10 HS-4 + ADR-013) plus user-kit markdown files per ADR-008. Boundary: per-Tenant isolated (HS-3 + ADR-006); cross-tenant calls require an explicit delegates_to edge; default-deny on cross-tenant data flow. Canon link: full daemon runtime ships at sutra/marketplace/native/bin/sutra-native + sutra/marketplace/native/src/ — path corrected 2026-05-13 per §10.10 P1 #5 (shipped runtime lives under sutra/marketplace/native/, not sutra/marketplace/plugin/).

mechanisms.title: §4.1 — 10 canon primitives
mechanisms.body: Native runtime uses 10 typed primitives per canon at sutra/os/native/primitives/: Domain, Charter, Workflow, Step, Trigger, ExecutionResult, EngineEvent, Tenant, Approval, DecisionProvenance — 'PRD body describes the operator-facing capability of each; engine type signatures + invariants + lifecycle live in canon.' What's NOT a primitive (older PRD had these): 'Agent' (agent behavior is composed from Workflow + Step + Charter scope + Authority gate), 'Method routing' (per-Step config + HOW Engine in §3), 'Audit substrate' (replaced by DecisionProvenance primitive + 3-channel ADR-013). Canon adds the engine-level facts: Workflow id is content-addressed W-hash (sha256 of canonical form — any field change yields a new Workflow id, immutable, new mint required); Step is skill_ref XOR action (I-3, mint-time HARD reject); ExecutionResult state is the 6-set {running, success, failed, awaiting_approval, paused, declared_gap} with failure_reason null IFF state ∈ {success, declared_gap} (I-4).

mechanisms.title: Execution lifecycle + terminal-event uniqueness (I-14)
mechanisms.body: Canon: 'every Execution has EXACTLY ONE terminal event from the set {workflow_completed, workflow_failed, approval_requested}'; rollback events (workflow_rollback_started → _complete | _partial) are RECOVERY transitions occurring AFTER workflow_failed under failure_policy='rollback' — they are NOT themselves terminal. Workflow lifecycle: Mint (LiteExecutor validates schema + invariants; content-addressed id; row persisted to user-kit registry) → Dormant → Triggered (TriggerSpec match or direct run CLI) → Running (preconditions cleared, workflow_started emits, step[0] dispatches) → step transitions → Terminal → Recovery (if rollback) → Decommission (registry entry deprecated=true prevents new Executions; existing Executions reach terminal independently; no field overwrite). ExecutionResult adds: when state === 'awaiting_approval', a persisted ledger row at user-kit/pending-approvals/E-<id>.json MUST exist (I-15); logs[] is append-only — never edit, never delete past events; partial=true ONLY when failure_policy='continue' advanced past a failed Step.

mechanisms.title: EngineEvent — append-only 26-event typed audit catalog
mechanisms.body: EngineEvent is 'Native's append-only typed audit row — one JSONL line per event', carrying event_type, ts_ms, execution_id?, payload, and agent_identity (per ADR-015); the catalog of 26 event_type values is exhaustive — new event-types require a NATIVE-ENGINE.md amendment + ADR, mint-time reject on unknown type. Invariants: monotonic ts_ms (replay safety — events must not be re-ordered after persistence); append-only immutability (replay derives full state from the log); per-event payload schema validation; I-16 commitment_broken referential integrity (must reference a resolvable Charter obligation id); I-9 + I-17 policy_decision must carry policy_id AND policy_version; execution_id may be null ONLY for events outside an Execution lifecycle (e.g. routing_decision pre-match). Sinks: ~/.sutra-native/user-kit/executions/E-<hash>.events.jsonl (per-Execution), user-kit/events.jsonl (global replay source), user-kit/decision-provenance.jsonl (DecisionProvenance subset), fsync-on-write per ADR-013. Master §4.11 deliberately does not duplicate the event names: 'readers should consult canon for the exhaustive list'.

mechanisms.title: 6 runtime surfaces — ROUTE · RUN · GATE · EMERGE · AUDIT · TENANT (RUN contract detail)
mechanisms.body: Per §4.11, the 6 surfaces are 'runtime interfaces between daemon + workflows + operator': ROUTE (operator utterance → Workflow selection), RUN (workflow execution — step machine + retry semantics), GATE (Authority + Approval), EMERGE (pattern propose/approve, ADR-010), AUDIT (DecisionProvenance + EngineEvent durable sink, ADR-013), TENANT (cross-tenant boundary, default-deny per ADR-006 + HS-3). RUN canon: fire a matched Workflow → dispatch each WorkflowStep → for action='invoke_host_llm' steps, hand the prompt to the configured host (claude --bare or codex exec) → persist a typed Execution log; reached via NativeEngine.run(workflowId, ctx) from handleHSutraEvent or via CLI 'sutra-native run <workflow-id>'. RUN invariants include: exactly one workflow_started per fired Workflow (RUN-I1); exactly one step_started per step dispatch (RUN-I2); per-step timeout_ms defaults to host-class default when null — 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s expected for complex codex tasks (RUN-I7). 'RUN executes within the Native daemon. The host-LLM session is the effector boundary (§5.1) — file/git/network mutations declared in the Workflow happen there, not in Native. Native persists EngineEvents; the host writes the actual side effects.' Declared canon gap: NativeEngine.on_host_llm_result resumption wire is open per §8 OS-1 — 'RUN's contract for awaiting that callback is implementation-shaped, not canon-shaped'.

mechanisms.title: §4.2 workforce state machine + §4.10.2 failure-state extensions
mechanisms.body: Happy path: PROPOSED (operator adds Charter) → operator approves → ACTIVE (Charter live) → new task (T0/T1/T2/T3) → agent materializes (scoped to Charter) → task completes → PERSISTED (artifact + audit row, output → B5.a/b/c/d) → operator revokes / scope-expires / supersedes → RETIRED (Charter inactive · audit replayable forever). §4.10.2 extends it with three failure states: PAUSED — entered when a hardstop fires or Charter Authority requires explicit operator decision; operator sees 'task paused at step X — decision needed'; exit via operator decision → ACTIVE (resume) or RETIRED (cancel). ESCALATED — entered when the B3 retry budget is exhausted (per §4.5) or the Authority gate triggers the ESCALATE class (ADR-018 contract 1); operator sees 'auto-retry exhausted; your judgment needed' with B3a THINK 3-angle brainstorm; exit via operator confirming direction → ACTIVE (B3b auto-executes) or RETIRED. DEGRADED — entered on connector half-failure (send succeeded but audit write missed) or partial side-effect; operator sees the partial-completion message with compensation options; exit via reconciliation step (idempotent retry or manual log-write) → ACTIVE or PAUSED.

mechanisms.title: §4.3 state envelope + §4.4 acceptance criteria
mechanisms.body: Pillar-to-pillar handoffs carry a typed envelope; CoS's 5 pillars consume + produce envelope fragments, and 'Native enforces shape + authority'. The envelope fields: turn_id, operator_id, charter_ref (which Charter scopes this turn), task_tier (T0/T1/T2/T3), intent {type, sub_intents} from B1, context_envelope {my_own, worlds_best, peer_sutras_v2} from B2, decision_trail [{phase, factors, authority_verdict, output_ref}] from B3, outbound [{audience, channel, draft, sent_status, inbound_responses}] from B4, b5_writes {active_session_ref, provenance_row_ref, learned_pattern_updates} to B5. §4.4 acceptance criteria (Native platform v1): Charter create/update/retire is operator-only and agent materialization is Native-internal; Authority gate fires at every external-effect call (send · write · delete · pay); the state envelope round-trips with zero data loss across pillar handoffs (HS-4 fires if it doesn't); audit substrate writes 100% of decisions to triple-channel (gate-log + provenance + artifact); cross-tenant queries default-deny.

mechanisms.title: §4.5 test-before-conclude gate (accuracy primitive)
mechanisms.body: 'Native does NOT mark a task done before testing the output. Accuracy is a per-workflow KPI. Test happens BEFORE concluding, not after. Output is rejected back to B3 retry if test fails.' Five steps: (1) pre-declare test per tier — T0 grep / file-exists / contract-match; T1 step-by-step verify + final integration check; T2 operator-visible 1-min iteration verification; T3 milestone-gate verification at goal-transition points; (2) B3 produces output (auto-execute path); (3) run the pre-declared test — 'Determinism: same input + same Charter → same expected output shape'; (4) conditional conclude — pass → conclude + write audit row + present to operator; fail → loop to B3 retry (max N retries per Charter), after N failures escalate to operator (Authority gate); (5) post-conclude — operator feedback (drop / accept / refine) becomes test signal for B5.d learned patterns, thresholds adapt per workflow. Rationale: testing before-conclude means 'CoS catches its own failures and retries silently'; the §7 accuracy KPI measures % of outputs passing first-time-test vs needing retry.

mechanisms.title: ADR-004 registry-and-effector split + ADR-005 host selection
mechanisms.body: ADR-004: 'Native engine MUST be the registry + audit layer; the founder's interactive host-LLM session MUST be the effector that performs declared mutations.' Native owns Workflow JSON, Trigger predicates, Execution rows, EngineEvent audit, DecisionProvenance, Tenant isolation; Claude (founder session) owns filesystem writes, git operations, network calls; the split is recorded on every Execution via the agent_identity chain (ADR-015). Consequences: daemon stays unauthenticated and recursion-safe (no credential exfil surface); audit records intent BEFORE the effector runs; autonomous 'fire-and-forget' workflows are blocked at v1.0 (deferred to v1.3 per OS-1/OS-2). ADR-005: 'Native engine MUST require WorkflowStep.host ∈ {claude, codex} whenever action='invoke_host_llm''. host='claude' invokes claude --bare (recursion-safe — recursive Claude without --bare re-loads the same governance pipeline, doubling token cost and potentially recursing forever); host='codex' invokes codex exec (read-only sandbox, default for analysis/review/planning). Per-step timeout_ms flows into host activity args; host-class defaults 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s for codex; the two-host set is locked in v1.x with an LLMSubstrate adapter deferred (OS-21). Steps needing BOTH authenticated mutation AND sandboxed analysis must split into two steps.

mechanisms.title: ADR-009 approval gate — typed pause + utterance-driven resume
mechanisms.body: ADR-009: 'Native engine MUST add requires_approval: bool at both Workflow and WorkflowStep levels, and emit/handle the typed event triplet approval_requested → approval_granted | approval_denied.' A step with requires_approval=true causes the executor to emit approval_requested, the Execution to transition to awaiting_approval, and a ledger row to persist at user-kit/pending-approvals/E-<id>.json (I-15) — the row survives daemon restart so pending approvals are recoverable. Founder utterance 'approve E-<id>' parses to NativeEngine.resumeApproved(execId) and continues at step_index+1; 'reject E-<id> <reason>' yields approval_denied and terminal workflow_failed. Re-fire on a resolved approval emits approval_already_handled — idempotent, keeping I-14's exactly-one-terminal contract. An inline Y/N stdin gate was rejected as physically impossible (daemon has no controlling TTY); an external approval-queue subsystem was rejected because splitting state across two registries makes replay ambiguous. Multi-party / quorum approval is deferred (OS-15).

mechanisms.title: ADR-011 on_failure policy — closed 5-set
mechanisms.body: ADR-011: 'Native engine MUST define step.on_failure as exactly one of {rollback, escalate, pause, abort, continue} — closed 5-set, no extension without ADR.' Effects per policy: rollback compensates steps in reverse and emits workflow_rollback_started → _complete or _partial; escalate emits workflow_escalated and routes to the founder channel; pause emits step_paused, persists a queue entry, resumes on signal; abort emits workflow_failed immediately; continue logs the failure, advances to step[i+1], sets partial=true, and skips outputs validation for the failed step. Workflow.failure_policy is the default; step.on_failure overrides per-step; each policy has a typed event family (events 4, 7, 19-24) — no free-form failure log. A boolean retry was rejected as too coarse; a custom callback per Workflow was rejected as non-deterministic and non-replayable. A sixth policy requires a new ADR + new event types + parser + executor branch — 'extension cost is deliberate'.

mechanisms.title: ADR-012 PNC predicates — typed parser, not trusted prose
mechanisms.body: ADR-012: 'Native engine MUST parse Workflow.preconditions, Workflow.postconditions, Workflow.failure_policy, and step.on_failure as typed machine-checkable predicates — not free prose.' Parser surface: match-all / match-any / cron / typed comparison against execution context (Tenant, Domain, Charter obligation id, prior EngineEvent). Evaluated at runtime via precondition_check (event 10) and postcondition_check (event 11); commitment_broken (event 25) references a Charter obligation id resolvable in the registry (I-16); F-10 forbids English-only routing/gating positions at terminal_check (HARD reject at primitive-mint). Evidence behind the decision: the 13-case run report showed prose PNC 'declared at primitive-mint but never eval-checked at runtime — silent guarantee failure'; LLM-eval of prose at runtime was rejected as non-deterministic, non-replayable, and an injection surface. A hybrid is allowed for documentation only: prose annotation is advisory per ADR-008, the typed core is load-bearing.

mechanisms.title: ADR-007 DecisionProvenance schema + ADR-013 fsync'd JSONL sink
mechanisms.body: ADR-007: 'Native engine MUST emit a typed DecisionProvenance row for every consequential decision (I-7), with policy_id AND policy_version non-empty (I-9, I-17).' Schema: id (uuid v4), ts_ms, agent_identity (chain), policy_id, policy_version, scope ∈ {WORKFLOW, STEP, HOOK, TENANT, CUTOVER}, outcome ∈ {allow, deny, pause, escalate}, reason (sanitized: no colons / no newlines), data_refs[] each carrying authoritative_status per ADR-008. PolicyDispatcher.evaluate(scope, evidence) returns the row; emitters append via UserKit.appendDecisionProvenance with fsync (ADR-013); DecisionProvenance is the replay surface — reconstructible by re-running the policy dispatcher on recorded evidence, and policy-version drift is detectable. ADR-013: EngineEvent and DecisionProvenance persist as fsync'd JSONL append-only files — one line per event, fsync per append, stderr beacon fallback when the primary path is unwritable, dual fallback to /tmp (the HS-4 chain); in-memory ring buffer and SQLite were rejected against the four constraints (survives restart, zero dependency, append-only audit, multi-process safe). The pattern detector (ADR-010) reads the log directly — no in-memory cache, restart-safe.

mechanisms.title: ADR-006 tenant isolation via Domain.tenant_id
mechanisms.body: ADR-006: 'Native engine MUST model tenant isolation as a first-class required field Domain.tenant_id (T-hash) referencing a Tenant primitive.' Every Domain belongs to exactly one Tenant (I-13, required field, no nullable); Execution.tenant_context carries {tenant_id} and TenantIsolation.assertCrossTenantAllowed(src, dst, op) is called unconditionally when a step touches a different tenant; cross-tenant ops without an explicit delegates_to edge fail closed and emit tenant_boundary_violation (HS-3, I-8). Cohort was rejected as the carrier because it is a routing/targeting primitive (a Workflow can target multiple Cohorts; a Domain belongs to exactly one Tenant); the D33 settings.json firewall stays as defense-in-depth at the Claude Code config layer — Native does NOT depend on it. The tenant boundary is a typed schema field checked at primitive-mint AND execution, and the audit trail records every cross-tenant attempt. Hierarchical/nested tenancy is declared in schema but execution semantics are v1.x backlog.

mechanisms.title: ADR-010 organic emergence — propose-approve at k≥4 (EMERGE surface)
mechanisms.body: ADR-010: 'Native engine MUST require explicit founder approval via approve P-<id> utterance to register any pattern-detected Workflow; the detector MUST propose only at k≥4 utterance matches.' The pattern detector reads the H-Sutra JSONL (ADR-013) and tracks per-pattern hit count + sample utterances; at k≥4 with no registered workflow matching, it emits pattern_proposed (event 12) with draft Workflow JSON + sample utterances; 'approve P-<id>' → proposal_approved (event 13) → register Workflow; 'reject P-<id> <reason>' → proposal_rejected (event 14). Auto-register was rejected (no founder oversight, no naming, no PNC review — 'can mint workflows from typos'); k=4 was set because 'k=2 is too noisy, k=3 still ambiguous, k=4 is the smallest k where a pattern is consistently a real workflow'. Sample utterances ship with the proposal so the founder can audit the matched evidence; smarter LLM-drafted Workflows on first match are deferred to v1.x backlog.

mechanisms.title: TriggerSpec primitive + ADR-017 cadence scheduling
mechanisms.body: TriggerSpec declares WHEN a Workflow fires: pattern ∈ {preprocessor, observer, gate, fan_out, negotiation} (closed 5-set), a typed predicate (match-all / match-any / cron — never free prose, HARD rejected at mint per ADR-012), target_workflow_id that MUST resolve in the user-kit registry (mint-time HARD reject if unresolved; non-firing if target later deprecated), and an optional cadence object per ADR-017. The Router consults Triggers for every HSutraEvent; on match it emits routing_decision (event 1) and dispatches NativeEngine.run(target_workflow_id, ctx); on miss it emits routing_decision with no matched_workflow_id or routes to the ADR-010 pattern-proposal flow when k≥4 unmatched utterances accumulate. Cadence-driven triggers fire via CadenceScheduler.tick() within ±5 min of schedule (I-12), each fire emitting EngineEvent + DecisionProvenance per ADR-017's daemon-side setInterval decision. Trigger terminal state is NOT specified in canon §2.5 — triggers are effectively permanent once minted in v1.0; a deprecated flag is a future-ADR implementation choice.

mechanisms.title: ADR-008 authoritative-vs-advisory status on every DataRef
mechanisms.body: ADR-008: 'Native engine MUST require every DataRef to carry an explicit authoritative_status ∈ {authoritative, advisory} field.' Readers honor authoritative over advisory at lookup time — declarative precedence, no convention; Workflow inputs[] and outputs[] tag each entry, enforced at primitive-mint via ajv schema validation; DecisionProvenance.data_refs[] carries the same field so every audit row records which version of which surface was load-bearing. The decision resolves the markdown-vs-code conflict: 'code always wins' breaks when markdown captures a NEW direction not yet wired; 'markdown wins' breaks when code is the live runtime contract; collapsing to one surface was rejected because the founder reads markdown and the daemon reads code. Drift detection runs as a weekly cadence reporting the authoritative-vs-advisory diff per artifact pair. Cost: every DataRef author must set the field — no implicit default, ajv rejects on omission.

mechanisms.title: ADR-014 depth router as Native's own Workflow (W-load-native-context)
mechanisms.body: ADR-014: 'Native engine MUST implement the depth-router as the W-load-native-context Workflow — fires codex exec, emits a structured load-plan JSON via return_contract, persists an Execution row.' The Workflow uses host='codex' (read-only sandbox per ADR-005) — analysis only, no mutation; inputs are turn context, depth signal, task class slug; outputs are a load-plan JSON {include: [paths], exclude: [paths], rationale} schema-validated by return_contract. Every depth-router fire is replayable from its Execution row; the pattern is 'the canonical example of Native runs Native', and reuse_tag=true makes it discoverable as a Skill via SkillEngine.resolve. Bash and inline-LLM alternatives were rejected for lacking audit rows, return_contract validation, and replay. Costs: per-fire Workflow boot + codex subprocess (~300ms baseline); a first fast-path measurement may force a hybrid (bash fast-path + Workflow slow-path).

mechanisms.title: ADR-022 full-loop six mechanisms (system-of-work science adoption)
mechanisms.body: ADR-022 (accepted 2026-06-12) adopts six dependency-ordered mechanisms: (1) SoR truth upgrade — bracket external effects with attempted/result events, persist LLM outputs AS events, deterministic replay, event schema versioning; (2) registration-at-birth — new workflow declares contract + reads/writes (→ where-used index) + version; (3) workflow authoring engine — observe situation → Cynefin classify → draft typed Workflow with per-step contracts → machine soundness check → ADR-010 propose/approve; (4) comparator + admission — reference limits per workflow + escalation, open-Execution WIP cap gates new runs; (5) the miner — scheduled read of the record proposing extraction/revision/retirement via propose/approve; (6) industry packs — templates + record schemas + reference limits per domain, 'engine stays domain-free'. The loop (design → execute → record → compare → redesign) closes at #5; sequence 1→2→3→4→5 with 6 parallel after 3. The honest-state finding: 'Native today runs design → execute → record. The record fails both litmus tests: not replayable (state cannot be rebuilt from the log alone) and not regulated (no decision rule reads it in-loop) — so the SoR is telemetry, not yet a system of record.' Mechanisms #3 and #5 each ship with their own ADR; charter Contract/Primitives edits land when #1/#2 ship.

mechanisms.title: §4.10.1 hardstop catalog HS-1..HS-8 + MECHANISM-PENDING hedge
mechanisms.body: 'Native's hardstop catalog (HS-1..HS-8) defines what the system does when it cannot continue safely'; the full engine spec lives at sutra/os/native/hardstops/HS-*.md and §4.10 is the operator-visible summary. Operator-visible behaviors: HS-1 system REFUSES to self-modify ('this change touches Sutra's own rules — please ratify directly'); HS-2 aborts the current turn when per-turn governance overhead exceeds 25% of token budget (canon HS-2 part-file: soft target ≤15% per I-6, HARD-STOP >25%, per-turn-scoped recovery — next turn proceeds normally); HS-3 cross-company action DENIED without explicit delegates_to; HS-4 system STOPS when DecisionProvenance is unwritable across all 3 fallback channels ('no silent unaudited execution'); HS-5 cutover PAUSED with operator + Tenant owner HITL; HS-6 SESSION SUSPENDED when 3+ distinct governance hooks fail in one turn; HS-7 shipment broadly BLOCKED when the codex review queue exceeds 20 items or any item is >7 days stale; HS-8 auto-ROLLBACK on production canary regression, founder notified. Hardstop UX contract: every hardstop produces a 1-2 sentence operator-facing message, a recommended NEXT ACTION, and a link to the audit row. The MECHANISM-PENDING callout (2026-05-13, §10.10 row 1): 'HS-4 · HS-5 · HS-6 · HS-7 · HS-8 are documented as canonical hardstops above, but the impl-vs-docs audit confirmed live detectors/executors do NOT yet exist in the shipped Native runtime — those rows are doctrine, mechanism pending. HS-1, HS-2, HS-3 have at least partial enforcement via existing plugin hooks.'

mechanisms.title: HS-9 keys-in-env-vars — canon DRAFT lesson-port from production PROTO-004
mechanisms.body: Canon hardstops/ contains a ninth part-file beyond master's HS-1..HS-8 list: HS-9 'Keys in env vars only' (DRAFT v1, authored 2026-06-12, 'lesson-port from ACTIVE production PROTO-004; not yet wired in Native runtime'). Fail-mode: 'Secrets live only in environment variables or env-type files. Any artifact write introducing a key-shaped string into a non-env file is denied at the boundary BEFORE the file is touched (exit-2 class block; the write never lands). Remediation edits that remove secrets always pass.' Two pattern families port verbatim because they catch disjoint cases: provider-shaped (sk-…, AKIA…, ghp_…, ghs_…, xoxb-…, ya29.…, AIza…, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY) and assignment-shaped (dispatcher Check-5). The two-pattern boundary reconciles §5.1 connector tokens: out-of-repo stores are a separately-governed sanctioned pattern — untracked, mode 0600, named location (~/.sutra-connectors/oauth/ precedent), edits gated by ADR-003 (deepseek MODIFY absorbed 2026-06-12); Native kill-switch key SUTRA_HS9_KEYS_DISABLED. Production dossier proto/004 confirms the contract is ACTIVE + HARD at two layers today (plugin keys-in-env-vars.sh PreToolUse exit-2 + holding dispatcher-pretool.sh Check 5), with an audited PROTO004_ACK override and the gap statement: 'Native names the hook in §4.11.A but states no key-handling invariant... Production has a precise, two-layer HARD contract... that Native has not captured as a hardstop' — now captured as this DRAFT part-file.

mechanisms.title: §4.8 Capability Surface Map (CSM) — feature lifecycle visible to operators
mechanisms.body: Native + CoS ship features through an explicit lifecycle; CSM is the source-of-truth for what's stable vs proposed, seen via the sutra-capability skill and SessionStart banner. States: cap-NNN PROPOSED (logged in CAPABILITY-MAP.md, not invocable) → CANDIDATE (under codex/deepseek review) → DESIGNED (architecture + acceptance ratified) → BUILT (merged, under §4.5 verification) → SHIPPING (verified, rolling out per §6.0 T1→T2→T3→T4 cadence) → LIVE/STABLE (default-on) → DEPRECATED (sunset per §6.4). The SHIPPING axis note (N38 resolution, 2026-06-12): 'this is the per-CAPABILITY rollout cadence — dogfood-first. It is a different axis from CLIENT-ONBOARDING order, which per D41 runs new-clients-first... Both hold; no contradiction.' Capability tiering across the fleet: L0 fleet-shipped (all T2-T4 via marketplace), L1 cohort-staged (with promotion deadline), L2 instance-local (T1 Asawa only — governance/experimental). Note: 'capabilities are atomic primitives; Modules (§1.4) are packaged compositions OF capabilities. CSM tracks both at different granularity.'

mechanisms.title: §4.9 module deployment — 3-artifact contract
mechanisms.body: A Module deploys via 3 artifacts — 'a conceptual contract first; filesystem layout below is one canonical implementation': SPEC (module code + manifest + JSON schema for binding + dependencies on platform Capabilities; sutra/marketplace/plugin/modules/<name>/; shared single-source-of-truth), BINDING (per-Deployment config: Charter scope, audience, authority thresholds, operator-set parameters; ~/.sutra/instances/<operator>/<company>/modules/<name>.json; per-Deployment overlay), RUNTIME STATE (executions, snapshots, logs, caches, audit rows, learned patterns; holding/state/modules/<name>/<tenant-id>/; per-Deployment isolated). Deployment flow: operator installs → BINDING created for this operator + Charter (Authority gate fires on first run) → Module runs → RUNTIME STATE accumulates in a per-tenant isolated subtree, audit rows → §2.B B5.c, metrics → §7. Acceptance criteria: SPEC update is operator-invisible (rolls in via plugin update per §6.4); BINDING is operator-editable within §1.4.3 deployment authority phases and Charter-scoped; RUNTIME STATE per-tenant isolated with cross-tenant access default-denied (the §4.9.2 row says 'HS-2 fires on violation'); retire/decommission pins SPEC, archives BINDING, preserves RUNTIME STATE for a replay window then trims per D.12 Artifact Governance.

mechanisms.title: Production dossier proto/002 — fan-out barrier/join rule (lesson for the Execution engine)
mechanisms.body: Production retired PROTO-002 as a protocol ('agent-execution concern, not a system invariant') but ships the lesson fleet-wide as plugin hook agent-completion-check.sh (PostToolUse on Bash|Edit|Write, SOFT exit-0): when heuristic signals of still-running parallel agents exist, the orchestrator gets the verbatim rule 'Do NOT write synthesis/output until ALL agents complete. Read ALL agent outputs before proceeding. Do NOT substitute your own work for pending agent work.' Redo recipe for Native: 'Native should NOT port the /tmp-mtime heuristic — it is a workaround for not owning the execution substrate. Native's daemon owns Execution rows with terminal states, so reimplement as a first-class barrier invariant: an orchestrating Execution may not transition to synthesis/terminal while any sibling_group member Execution is non-terminal; on violation, block or queue rather than warn.' The dossier ports the doctrine sentence and two origin incidents (Maze HOD 2026-04-04 orchestrator wrote report over 3 running agents and missed 6 bugs; Dharmik SEO 2026-04-07 compiled before 4 agents returned) as rationale. Gap vs Native: 'Native has sibling_group lineage and B13 artifact locks but no stated barrier/join rule.'

mechanisms.title: Production dossier hook/check-graduation — SOFT→HARD promotion pipeline constants
mechanisms.body: Production ships a 3-script graduation framework: compliance-tracker.sh appends {ts,hook,status} JSONL rows per SOFT-hook pass/warn; check-graduation.sh computes per-hook pass% and prints GRADUATE (promote to HARD) when total ≥20 events AND pass <80%, KEEP SOFT at ≥80%, WAITING under 20 events — report-only, never flips enforcement itself; resilience.sh tracks consecutive fails, persisting state + warning at 2 consecutive and auto-escalating to a founder-visible os/feedback-to-sutra/ file at ≥3. Redo recipe: 'Port the constants verbatim: 20-event observation window, 80% compliance threshold, 2-consecutive persist / 3-consecutive escalate. Redesign the plumbing as Native primitives: every SOFT-policy evaluation emits a pass/warn EngineEvent into a compliance stream...; a graduation evaluator (workflow or scheduled job) computes per-policy verdicts...; resilience escalation becomes an event-threshold rule.' Promotion stays founder-gated — the only real flip that ever happened (2026-05-10 marker hooks) was founder-directed manual, so 'the framework's role is evidence-for-decision, not auto-promotion'. Gap vs Native: 'Native defines SOFT/HARD/CONVENTION tiers but has no promotion pipeline between them: no compliance event stream, no numeric graduation thresholds or observation window, no GRADUATE/KEEP/WAITING report, and no consecutive-failure escalation path.'

mechanisms.title: Production dossier proto/023 — per-instance runtime config surface (kill-switch registry)
mechanisms.body: Production ships one shell-sourceable file per instance at $HOME/.sutra/config.env holding every kill-switch, threshold, and opt-in, plus a bin/sutra-config CLI (get / set / list / init / path; init idempotent; set preserves inline comments). Default config ships kill-switches (SUTRA_RTK_ENABLED, SUTRA_CODEX_DIRECTIVE_ENABLED, SUTRA_ESTIMATION_COLLECTOR_ENABLED, SUTRA_COMPLETION_PROTOCOL_ENABLED), thresholds (SUTRA_CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS=600000, SUTRA_DEPTH_DEFAULT=5, SUTRA_BUILD_LAYER_DEFAULT=L0), observability (SUTRA_TELEMETRY=off), and tier (SUTRA_TIER=governance); config is ADDITIVE — existing env-var overrides keep working. Redo recipe: 'Native's typed declarative config (B10/P10) covers schema but not the operational knob surface — reimplement as a Native-owned per-instance runtime config: one sourceable/parseable file the daemon AND host-side hooks both read, holding the kill-switch registry, thresholds, and tier'; port the SUTRA_ key-prefix convention, UPPERCASE key validation, and additive compat rule verbatim; redesign the CLI as a sutra-native subcommand; and 'mandate (and lint) that every Native hardstop/hook declares its kill-switch key in this registry — production never closed the adoption loop (1 of ~75 hooks sources it).' Gap vs Native: 'No sutra-config, config.env, or kill-switch-registry concept is traced in Native.'

mechanisms.title: §4.6 HOW bridge + §4.7 workforce outputs as deliverables
mechanisms.body: §4.6: every Native primitive embeds a HOW choice from §3 — Charters declare HOW preferences at creation, agents materialize with HOW context inherited, method routing (D.11) implements HOW-tier mapping, the authority gate (D.6) defers to HOW's escalation logic; 'Native runtime is the executor; §3 HOW is the doctrine.' §4.7: the workforce produces software + agentic systems with three delivery destinations — D1 shipped to client (client owns; Native deletes its copy post-handoff), D2 shipped back to Sutra-org (ratified into plugin/platform per §6 lifecycle), D3 operator-internal use (operator keeps in their Native workspace). The delivery pipeline is owned by §6 Distribution — '§4.7 declares the platform CAPABILITY...; §6 owns the delivery modes'; all deliverables emit DecisionProvenance + D.12 Artifact Governance metadata (version, owner, source-Charter, audit trail).

mechanisms.title: §3 section contract — purpose, ownership, boundary
mechanisms.body: §3 is "Native's IP: not 'do the work' — 'do the work via the right way of looking at this task.'" It owns the Lens primitive, the axes (Realization + Reflection as the recommended pair; many others available), the value-is-an-axis recursion, the examples, the decision procedure, and the operator-facing surface of HOW. It depends on §2 task tier (T0-T3), §4 Native runtime (where Lens choices manifest), and §7 Observability (where Lens accuracy is measured). It does NOT own execution (§4 runtime), operator surface (§2), transport (§5), or "the DAG / build / Native-primitive implementation (Claude-suggested, archived — not committed design)." One-sentence theory: every piece of design knowledge is a "way of looking" (a Lens); there are many possible lenses, not capped; the two recommended for building anything are Realization (abstract idea → running thing) and Reflection (instance → axis → meta-axis → … → grammar). The section self-declares: "This section is THEORY work; productization is the next step."

mechanisms.title: §3.1 The atom — a value is just an axis
mechanisms.body: The smallest move is classification: a value is an item; an axis is a set of values. The role is RELATIVE to level — "a thing is a VALUE seen from the axis above it; the same thing is an AXIS seen from the values below it." "Value" and "axis" are the same kind of object viewed from one level up or down. This is the only primitive; everything else is this move repeated. Formal grounding cited by the master: type-universe relativity; Tarski's object-language / meta-language stratification.

mechanisms.title: §3.2 Axes — many possible, two recommended; the coupling rule
mechanisms.body: An axis is a particular Lens — one way of looking at the thing being built; there can be MANY axes (viewpoint · concern · time · ownership · scale · certainty · …) and "you are not capped to any number. You pick the lenses that change a decision for this idea and ignore the rest." The two recommended axes: Realization (abstract idea → concrete running thing; example values worldview · vision · strategy · capability · architecture · feature · contract · implementation) and Reflection (instance → axis → meta-axis → method → framework → paradigm → grammar; M0-M6, the recursion uncapped). Other available lenses are added per idea only if they change a decision: viewpoint (user / system / governance), concern (security / cost / accuracy), time (past / now / next / later · v1 / v2 / v3), ownership (human / AI / human-in-loop), scale (fleet / cohort / instance). Coupling of the recommended pair: "as you ascend Reflection to mint a structure (an axis, a schema), the forward Realization journey then consumes that structure instead of re-deriving it. Climb to write a schema once; descend and every instance conforms. The abstraction is carried forward as an input, not copied."

mechanisms.title: §3.3 Dynamic — nothing is capped; three stop rules
mechanisms.body: The number of Realization levels and Reflection heights is NOT fixed; it is decided per idea. Dimensions are generated, not listed: each dimension = (interrogative × mechanism) — a finite generator mints an open set on demand. Realization stops by atomicity (downward — stop decomposing at the smallest buildable unit); Reflection stops by reflexivity (upward — stop climbing at the level that describes itself); both stop by the decision test (the practical cap): add a level or a dimension only while it still changes what you build or who reads it. Callout: "Possibility is not obligation. The space is astronomic; you instantiate only the corner a destination needs."

mechanisms.title: §3.4 Worked examples — Realization walk, time axis, nD lenses, 6×7 cross, one-to-many cells, nD projection
mechanisms.body: Example 1 walks one idea down Realization: worldview "operator sovereignty" → vision → strategy → capability → architecture (B1 Intent block inside the CoS layer) → feature (B1 intake: capture → classify → conf-gate → log → route) → contract intent{type, confidence, routed_to, clarify} → implementation (classifier prompt + intake_log.jsonl + emit). Example 2 shows the time axis on the same thing (past: no formal intake · v1: single LLM call, conf-gate 0.6 · v2: eval-tuned 0.75 + golden-set CI · v3: voice + screenshot multi-modal). Example 4 renders the recommended pair as a clean 6×7 cross (Worldview…Implementation × M0 instance…M6 grammar), read left→right as "a concrete thing → the axis it belongs to → the axis-of-axes → the method that produces them → the framework hosting the method → the paradigm → the reflexive grammar." Example 5 states the cross is many-to-many, not 1-to-1 — each cell is a SET of candidates and "a build decision is the act of picking one (or a few) from each relevant cell" — with 5a expanding the M3 method column (e.g. Architecture: C4 model · Zachman framework · 4+1 views · ADR pattern · arc42) and 5b expanding the Architecture row as a fan-out tree across all 7 Reflection levels (M0: 5-layer architecture · 6 surfaces ROUTE/RUN/GATE/EMERGE/AUDIT/TENANT · 10 primitives · 26 EngineEvents · 8 hardstops). Example 6 catalogs six established techniques for showing >2 axes (small multiples/Tufte, parallel coordinates/Inselberg, heatmap, faceted filter/Ranganathan, hierarchical nested headers, 3D cube + slices) with the punchline: "you don't visualize nD directly. You project. Every diagram is a 2D projection of an n-dimensional address space."

mechanisms.title: §3.5 Decision procedure with Lenses (6 steps + worked decision)
mechanisms.body: A decision is choosing which lens to apply; a good decision is one that changes the path to your destination — "the framework's biggest gift is telling you which decisions you do not have to make yet." The six steps: 1 ANCHOR (name the destination; no destination → no decision) · 2 ON-PATH? (if not in the destination's required sub-graph → DEFER; "Most 'decisions' die here") · 3 LEVEL (find the decision's level/dimension and pick the matching lens — "Decide architecture with the architecture lens, not the implementation lens") · 4 REAL? (do options lead to DIFFERENT downstream sub-graphs? if not, pick either and move on) · 5 WEIGH (reversible → decide fast, revise later; irreversible → apply MULTIPLE lenses; "where the lenses DISAGREE is the actual tradeoff to resolve") · 6 RECORD (node + provenance: destination, lenses used, choice, why). The worked decision "B1 classifier: single LLM call vs fine-tuned model?" resolves to single-call for v1 — reversible-ish (intent{} contract unchanged either way), lenses [cost, time, accuracy, reversibility] agree, with recorded revisit trigger "if eval pass-rate drops below 90%." Net effect per the master: eliminates off-path agonizing (step 2), false decisions (step 4), wrong-level thrash (step 3); adds effort calibrated to reversibility, multi-lens only for the genuinely hard ones, and replayable rationale.

mechanisms.title: §3.6 The 6 HOW dimensions — operator-facing surface
mechanisms.body: The 6 dimensions are the operator-facing surface of §3.2's axes — the specific lenses an operator picks when working with Native today; each row reads "what the operator is choosing" and "the values available." Approach: top-down (goal → factors → tasks), bottom-up (data → patterns → conclusion), or by analogy (this looks like prior X). Mindset: optimize (maximize known metric) · explore (surface options) · repair (fix broken state) · audit (verify-only). Structure: tree of sub-tasks (T3 Charter decomposition) · sequential pipeline (T1 multi-action) · parallel scan (T2 iterative) · iteration loop (refinement). Detailing: coarse first pass + sharpen (T0/T1 fast iterations) vs fully detailed from start (T3 charter with locked requirements). Decomposition: 3-factor (forced parsimony) / 7-factor (completeness) / by-stakeholder (comms-heavy) / by-deliverable / by-risk (high-stakes). Cascading: when a sub-task gets stuck, recurse on the sub-task — a sub-T3 spawns a child T3 with its own Lens choices, depth bounded by complexity budget.

mechanisms.title: §3.7 Lens selection flow → lens manifest in state envelope
mechanisms.body: Selection takes operator intent (B1) + task tier (T0-T3) as input. The LENS SELECTION block runs five steps: 1. read Charter scope (§4 primitive) · 2. read past patterns from B5.d · 3. choose lens values (approach · mindset · structure · detailing · decomposition) · 4. estimate complexity → cascade depth · 5. declare lens choice to operator (B3a if explicit; silent if known). Output: "lens manifest emitted into state envelope (§4.3); §4 Native runtime executes." If a sub-task gets stuck the flow recurses lens selection (cascade) with depth--. The master maps this flow onto the §3.5 decision procedure: Anchor → Level → Real? → Weigh → Record.

mechanisms.title: §3.8 Cross-section presence — lenses are everywhere
mechanisms.body: Per the §3.8 table: §2.B B1 (Ask my way) parses the operator's lens preferences from utterance (e.g., "quickly" = coarse-first detailing). §2.B B3a (THINK) brainstorm partnership uses Explore mindset and declares its lens choice before deepening; §2.B B3b (DO) auto-execute uses Optimize mindset by default and switches to Repair when output fails verification. In the §4 Native runtime, the lens manifest in the state envelope binds method routing (§9 D.11), agent scope, and token budget. §4.5 test-before-conclude's verification step is itself a lens choice (audit mindset · by-deliverable decomposition). §6 Distribution/onboarding surfaces + ratifies the operator's first-week lens preferences during Charter setup. §7 Observability carries the Lens accuracy KPI — operator drop rate per lens choice; drift signals on method-route accuracy.

mechanisms.title: §4.6 HOW Methodology bridge — runtime executor vs §3 doctrine
mechanisms.body: Master §4.6 (cross-reference): "Every Native primitive (§4.1) embeds a HOW choice from §3 HOW Methodology. Charters declare HOW preferences at creation; agents materialize with HOW context inherited; method routing (D.11) implements HOW-tier mapping; authority gate (D.6) defers to HOW's escalation logic. Native runtime is the executor; §3 HOW is the doctrine." The §1 architecture cross-cut table carries the identical contract as its "HOW / method-routing bridge" row, adding that HOW-tier mapping means "different problem classes get different solving strategies, per B3b DO." §2's task-taxonomy callout feeds the same bridge: "Method selection (D.11) chooses different intelligence per tier." D.11 Method Selection itself is a Native platform primitive with its own per-tier method-profile table (T0 speed/fast model · T1 reliability/per-step verify · T2 responsiveness/1-min loop · T3 long-horizon quality/best model + ensemble) — its primary home is master §9 Meta (governance band), so the HOW page cites it rather than restating it.

mechanisms.title: §3.9 Acceptance criteria (theory v1)
mechanisms.body: Forward-looking note verbatim: "this section is THEORY work; productization is the next step. v1 ships the doctrine + the Lens primitive + the recommended axes; v2+ will lock the surface and refine based on dogfood signal." Four criteria: (1) every Native turn carries an explicit lens manifest in state envelope (operator can request "show me your lenses"); (2) lens choices learned from B5.d learned patterns improve future selections (drift signal triggers re-learning); (3) cascade depth bounded by complexity budget (Charter-set); depth-exhaustion escalates to operator (Authority gate); (4) operator can override any lens choice; override learned + applied to future similar tasks.

mechanisms.title: §3.A + §3.Z Provenance — founder-prompt origins and fold note
mechanisms.body: §3.A preserves the 25 founder prompts that shaped §3 per founder direction 2026-05-31 — "every PRD artifact carries the originating prompts so the reasoning trail is replayable" — with speech-to-text slips bracketed (e.g. "access [axes]"); a persistent prompts log lives at holding/state/prompts/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl, auto-captured via the L0 plugin hook capture-prompt.sh (v2.39.6+). §3.Z records the fold: §3 was folded 2026-05-31 from the staging doc how-methodology.html, archived at holding/research/_archive/native-v1.x/2026-05-28-how-methodology-staging.html; the Claude-suggested DAG/Implementation/Operating-loop sections were preserved there and NOT folded into §3 per founder direction "theory, productization later." Sources borrowed per the footer: faceted classification (Ranganathan), morphological analysis (Zwicky), MDSOC / "N degrees of separation" (Tarr et al.), MOF metamodel layers, type universes, Zachman, Tufte, Inselberg.

mechanisms.body: The 2026-05-13 implementation-vs-documentation audit (codex Lane A + DeepSeek Lane A, independent runs) records convergent-gap row 5: "HOW Methodology (§3) has zero runtime enforcement." How are HOW choices learned vs. operator-overridden? When are HOW choices made silently vs. surfaced for ratification?" packs.subsystem: platform-observability (platform/observability.html — §7 Observability: daily pulse · coverage · token efficiency)

mechanisms.title: §7 section contract — purpose, ownership, boundary
mechanisms.body: Purpose: "Instrument every layer so operator + Asawa team can see whether CoS is doing what it promises, and where it's drifting." Owns: per-pillar quality metrics · drift signals · operator satisfaction signals · audit + replay surfaces. Depends on: all layers (instruments cross-cuttingly). Does NOT own: decision execution; transport; pricing. Master §4.0's canon-link adds: "Operator-visible health surface lives in §7 Observability." The UI-block second-order draft restates the doc-home: §7 "owns per-pillar quality metrics, drift signals, operator satisfaction signals (incl. skill-mode misdetection rate per a9-skill-modes), audit + replay surfaces; depends on all layers (instruments cross-cuttingly per §1.1 layer diagram)."

mechanisms.title: §7.1 Per-pillar metrics + drift signals
mechanisms.body: Each pillar carries one primary metric and one drift signal: B1 Ask my way — intent parse accuracy (intent_type + sub-intents match operator's correction frequency); correction rate >15% per week → drift. B2 World's best + mine — context relevance (operator drops <10% of retrieved context); drop rate >25% → drift. B3 Think + Do + Present — auto-vs-ask ratio; outcome quality (operator accepts >80% of B3b outputs); accept rate falls >15pp WoW. B4 Talk for me — outbound success rate; audience-calibration accuracy; operator overrides voice >20% of sends. B5 Remember — replay latency (≤30s/day-window v1) + cross-tenant default-deny verified; replay latency >60s OR any cross-tenant leak. §3.8 additionally registers a Lens accuracy KPI in §7: "operator drop rate per lens choice; drift signals on method-route accuracy" (§3's header names §7 as "where Lens accuracy is measured").

mechanisms.title: §7.1.A Accuracy KPI — integration with §4.5 test-before-conclude
mechanisms.body: Four metrics with v1 targets and drift signals: first-time-test pass rate (% of CoS outputs passing the pre-declared §4.5 test on first try) — ≥85% T0, ≥75% T1, ≥65% T2, ≥55% T3 Charter milestones; drift on drop >10pp WoW per task tier. Retry-to-conclude ratio — ≤1.3 T0, ≤2.0 T1, ≤3.0 T2/T3; drift when ratio rises >0.5 WoW. Escalation rate (test-fail-exhausted) — ≤5% across all tiers; >10% any tier → workflow review. Post-conclude operator-correction rate — ≤8% T0/T1, ≤15% T2/T3; rate rises → test criteria need tightening. Callout verbatim: "Accuracy is a per-workflow KPI, not a single number. Each task tier (T0-T3) + each pillar carries its own accuracy band. §4.5 Test-before-conclude is where the test runs; §7.1.A is where the aggregated results live." §4.5's side of the contract: "Accuracy KPI in §7 Observability measures: % of CoS outputs that passed first-time-test vs needed retry." The SoP second-order draft carries this as its outbound Observability contract row, adding "daemon health surfaced only via Daily Pulse health row" and platform-health instrumentation. FQ2 (PROPOSED 2026-05-13, not ratified) holds the forward open questions: KPIs per tier, right test depth per phase, test-before-conclude vs test-by-sample cost tradeoff, accuracy compounding vs degrading over time.

mechanisms.title: §7.2 Audit + replay surfaces — the 5-artifact per-turn trail
mechanisms.body: "The audit promise of B5.c made visible. Every Native turn produces 5 artifacts; observability surfaces all 5 to operator on demand": 1. INTENT RECORD (B1 — parsed intent + sub-intents + schema preview) · 2. CONTEXT MANIFEST (B2 — ranked artifact list used; what was dropped) · 3. DECISION PROVENANCE (B3 — phases + factors + authority verdict + output) · 4. OUTBOUND LOG (B4, if comms triggered — audience + channel + draft + sent + replies) · 5. SUBSTRATE WRITE (B5 — active-session ref + learned-pattern updates). Operator commands: "replay last Paisa turn" → all 5 artifacts shown chronologically; "show me what changed in B5.d this week" → diff of learned patterns. The SoR second-order draft mirrors this as a stored-data row ("Per-turn 5-artifact audit trail — every Native turn produces 5 stored artifacts") and as its outbound Observability contract row: all 5 per-turn artifacts replayed on demand, replay ≤30s for a single-day window, learned-pattern diffs, B5 drift signals (replay latency >60s OR any cross-tenant leak).

mechanisms.title: §7.3 Operator satisfaction signals
mechanisms.body: Four signals, verbatim from master: time-to-decision (operator decides on CoS output in <30s — CX bar gate); refusal-to-execute rate (operator says "don't do this, ask me first"); autonomy-dial direction (does operator dial autonomy up or down per domain over time?); surface-switching frequency (operator should NOT switch surfaces mid-task per CX bar).

mechanisms.title: §7.4 Acceptance criteria (Observability v1) + the HS-4 dependency
mechanisms.body: Three criteria: (1) 5-artifact audit trail emitted per turn — HS-4 fires on any missing channel; (2) operator can request replay for any past turn within ≤30s for a single-day window; (3) drift signals tracked weekly; breach surfaces to founder via Daily Pulse. HS-4 canon (primary home: platform-runtime hardstops; cited here because §7.4 depends on it): fires when the DecisionProvenance JSONL audit log is unwritable across all 3 channels — primary fsync'd append (ADR-013), stderr beacon, /tmp dual fallback; fail-mode "block all governance hooks; stderr beacon"; downstream, "audit-trail integrity preserved by blocking, not by writing without trace"; STRIDE class Repudiation / audit-trail loss. Master carries the MECHANISM-PENDING hedge (added 2026-05-13 per §10.10 row 1): HS-4..HS-8 "are documented as canonical hardstops... but the impl-vs-docs audit confirmed live detectors/executors do NOT yet exist in the shipped Native runtime — those rows are doctrine, mechanism pending."

mechanisms.title: AUDIT surface — canon persistence + replay subsystem
mechanisms.body: Canon: "Every state transition across every surface emits exactly one typed EngineEvent + (for consequential decisions) one DecisionProvenance row. AUDIT is the persistence + replay surface for those rows." AUDIT is not directly invoked — ROUTE/RUN/GATE/EMERGE/TENANT call UserKit.appendDecisionProvenance(dp) (§3.1) or emit EngineEvent rows AUDIT persists. Read-side surfaces: DecisionProvenance JSONL (append-only telemetry sink §5.6); EngineEvent JSONL per Tenant at Tenant.audit_log_path (§2.8); replay surface §6.1 — every consequential decision rebuildable from agent_identity + policy_id + policy_version + data_refs + outcome. Eight invariants AUDIT-I1..I8: ≥1 EngineEvent per transition; exactly one DecisionProvenance per consequential decision (I-7); ts_ms monotonic per process; reason field sanitized (no colons, no newlines) for JSONL parseability; durability via fsync per append + 3-channel fallback + stderr beacon last-resort; HS-4 fail-CLOSED ("if AUDIT cannot write, governance halts"); policy_id + policy_version non-empty on every row (F-8 + I-9); agent_identity chain-shaped per ADR-015. AUDIT persists all 26 EngineEvent types of §3.2 (full catalog enumerated in the part-file; one canon part-file per event exists under sutra/os/native/events/). mechanisms.title: ADR-013 — telemetry sink: fsync'd JSONL append
mechanisms.body: Decision: "Native engine MUST persist EngineEvent and DecisionProvenance as fsync'd JSONL append-only files; H-Sutra event bus MUST follow the same shape." Mechanics: one JSONL line per event/decision; UTF-8; no newline-in-field (sanitized at emit); fsync per append — never lose a row on crash; stderr beacon fallback when primary path is unwritable; dual fallback to /tmp (HS-4 chain); the pattern detector (ADR-010) reads the log directly — no in-memory cache, restart-safe. Alternatives rejected: in-memory ring buffer (fails restart-survival — codex P1.2 forced rejection) and SQLite/DB (adds dependency + schema migrations). Consequences: crash-safe; zero new runtime dependency; multi-process safe (POSIX append atomicity for short lines); disk I/O cost per event accepted at current rate; no indexed query — replay is sequential scan, aggregation is downstream tooling; OTel production transport (OS-10) is the next-tier deferral, JSONL stays primary.

mechanisms.title: North Star metric — Operator-Hours-Saved per week (OHS/wk)
mechanisms.body: Canon definition: "Hours per week the operator NO LONGER thinks about, because Native handled them — audit-derived from auto-run lifecycle phases + operator weekly confirmation." Why this metric: captures unit-of-value (time); measurable; leading indicator of retention; aligns with JTBD outcomes #1+#2 (minimize time + variance); works at any scale. Two-channel measurement per NATIVE-ENGINE §11.2: (a) audit-derived — auto-run lifecycle Executions × completion-time × non-trivial gate; (b) operator self-report — weekly survey. Cadence: weekly aggregation; per-operator + per-tenant roll-up. Leading inputs: workflows successfully auto-run after operationalization (count/wk), pattern proposals approved (precision ≥75%), cross-company decisions replayable from audit log ≥99% (DecisionProvenance log completeness 100% of consequential decisions), operator weekly active sessions trending up over 12 weeks, time-to-first-Execution ≤30 min (I-11). Targets table compiled below; 5-year targets marked "illustrative for direction; founder reviews + tunes at quarterly OKR cycle."

mechanisms.title: §7.5 Daily Pulse — operator's daily aggregate dashboard (Module per §1.4)
mechanisms.body: Daily Pulse is the visible artifact of §2.E S5 whole-system state, auto-generated by holding/hooks/observability-synthesis.sh from session-end data; operator reads once/day to see what CoS did + drift signals across the portfolio. Hierarchy tag: a Module per §1.4 Product Hierarchy — composes cap-Telemetry + cap-Audit + cap-CrossPortfolio-Priority; independent lifecycle; per-Deployment BINDING (operator config: pulse cadence, channel, signal thresholds); own RUNTIME STATE (daily-pulse archive per tenant); "reusable across future products on Native (designed for, not guaranteed v1)." Contents: 7 sections (per-Charter status · cross-portfolio priority via §3 HOW + §6 importance ranking · accuracy snapshot per §7.1.A with WoW trend · workforce health · feedback summary · token/RTK efficiency · outstanding gates per D.6) — full table below. Operator commands: /asawa (CEO dashboard), /status (session status + drift signals); delivery via holding/OBSERVABILITY-PULSE.md + optional email/Slack push per Charter. Acceptance (§7.5.3): pulse auto-generates within 60s of session-end; operator scans + decides in ≤2 minutes (CX bar gate per D.7); drift breach surfaced visually (boxed callout); cross-portfolio priorities ranked by Charter weight + recency + risk per §3 HOW decomposition. Stated sources line: holding/OBSERVABILITY-PULSE.md · holding/ANALYTICS-PULSE.md · observability-synthesis.sh · holding/scripts/daily-review.sh · founder direction "cadence is hours not days" — manifest acceptance: live telemetry scripts cited, not copied.

mechanisms.title: Coverage engine — shipped five-layer process-coverage system (production dossier)
mechanisms.body: Production ships a complete, live process-coverage system in five layers: (1) spec — COVERAGE-ENGINE.md with a depth-indexed expected checklist (D1=4, D2=7, D3=14, D4=19, D5=24 method IDs), the coverage-log.jsonl row schema {task, depth, method, ts, evidence, skipped_reason, override}, the evidence-specificity rule ("if your evidence could describe any task, it's not evidence"), and a SOFT-to-HARD ladder; (2) machine-readable contract — os/method-registry.jsonl encoding all 26 methods with id/category/min_depth/required_at[depths]/phase/conditional; (3) writers — log-coverage.sh HARD-rejects any runtime skip (5th arg → exit 2, per D31 "clients execute, never skip") and auto-coverage.sh fires on PostToolUse(Edit|Write|Bash), declaratively mapping paths/commands to methods with per-turn dedupe (the dominant production writer, not LLM discipline); (4) gate + report — coverage-gate.sh at Stop computes expected = enabled_methods ∩ required_at[depth] and prints the missing list SOFT (always exit 0); coverage-report.sh emits OK/SKIP/MISS/COND with status bands (EXCELLENT≥90 / GOOD≥70 / CONCERN≥50 / CRITICAL<50), bonus methods never inflating the score; (5) aggregation — observability-synthesis.sh (3h launchd) derives coverage-fires-per-commit, RED when commits>0 but fires=0. Redo recipe for Native: port the method registry verbatim as a Native SoR table; reimplement the writer as EngineEvent emission in the daemon (declarative path-glob/command-substring → method data, daemon-owned dedupe); reimplement gate + report as queries over events; keep SOFT-first with codified HARD triggers (per-method fire rate >85% stable 90 days → individually HARD-gate; <60% session coverage → block checkpoint); "surface coverage-per-commit as the §7 Observability process-adherence KPI." Dossier confidence: high; live log verified (43 rows, latest 2026-06-11).

mechanisms.title: Coverage enablement authority — D31 (production dossier)
mechanisms.body: The D31 dossier mechanizes "only Sutra flips switches": a per-client enabled_methods block in os/SUTRA-CONFIG.md is marked "Sutra-managed, do not edit manually," defaults false for every new method (clients with no block = all methods disabled), with the live asawa instance enabling all 26 registry methods. log-coverage.sh had its runtime skip path REMOVED 2026-04-20 — passing a 5th (skip_reason) argument exits 2 with stderr instructing the client to either fire the method or file feedback at os/feedback-to-sutra/; "clients literally cannot skip at runtime." coverage-gate.sh runs at Stop computing enabled_methods ∩ required_at_depth — SOFT Phase 1, with HARD Phase 2 (Stop-event block + COVERAGE_OVERRIDE=1 audited escape) and Phase 3 telemetry-driven review specified. Redo recipe: per-tenant capability switches (default false) in platform-owned tenant config; an execution logger with no runtime-skip parameter (port the reject-skip block verbatim — "it is the heart of the direction"); do NOT port PROTO-018 (retired) — redesign flip distribution on Native's plugin-version push; keep the three-phase SOFT→HARD→telemetry hardening schedule. Gap vs Native: only a one-line clause in section-10.5; the mechanism is unspecified in the runtime and section-6.7; maps to requirement N36.

mechanisms.title: Fleet consumption dashboard — fleet.sh (production dossier)
mechanisms.body: Production ships holding/departments/analytics/fleet.sh (178 lines) — "the 'who is running the plugin, right now' dashboard." Data source: ~/.sutra/sutra-data-cache/ (local clone of private repo sankalpasawa/sutra-data), populated by client /sutra-push events from telemetry-opt-in installs, each contributing clients/<install_id>/manifest.json; rows parse to {install_id, github_login, git_user_name, os_pretty, arch, tz, project_name, push_count, sutra_version, last_seen, age_days, has_identity}. Three modes: all installs (default), --fresh (last_seen ≤7 days = active), --id <prefix> single-install detail; output is 5 aggregates (total installs, identified count/%, unique github logins, unique humans, total pushes) plus a per-install table, with a printed privacy caveat — outbound telemetry DISABLED by default since plugin v2.0.0 per PRIVACY.md. Embedded ops thresholds: warn on active-install drop >25% WoW and identified <70%; breach when 0 installs (push pipeline broken); migration trigger fleet >50 → hosted dashboard. Redo recipe: port the manifest.json interchange shape verbatim (it is the contract between client push and fleet view); redesign the renderer as a Native query over the telemetry SoR producing the same 5 aggregates + active-within-7-days filter; keep the privacy default and carry the ops thresholds as monitoring rules. Gap vs Native: Native has telemetry collection (ADR-013) and the tier taxonomy, but the fleet-level aggregate consumption view is unspecified — "only partner-fleet observability appears, and only as a backlog criterion."

mechanisms.title: Speed charter — latency profiling + governance-overhead budget (production dossier)
mechanisms.body: Production ships a three-part solution: (1) SPEED.md charter (ACTIVE) with the Iron Rule "No Speed improvement ships without a cited time-sink baseline from this charter's data. Guess-driven cuts are blocked," 8 KPI formulas with Warn/Breach thresholds (governance overhead % = sum of routing+depth+hook+boot phases / task wall time, target <15%, breach ≥30% auto-becomes the #1 cut), a 6-wave gated roadmap (taxonomy → instrument → collect 2 weeks zero-change → RCA → founder-approved proposals → ship+measure → propagate), an anti-pattern table (cache-by-feel, single-run optimization, killing governance for speed all banned), and a satisfied-closure clause; (2) SPEED-phase-taxonomy.md with the full phase tree, per-phase start/end boundary-event table, governance-overhead summation formula, 8 collector invariants (I1: sum(phase_ms) within ±2% of wall), and the canonical LATENCY-LOG.jsonl row schema; (3) latency-collector.sh — a Stop-hook collector appending one row per task (wall_ms, tool counts, full token usage incl. cache_read/cache_creation, partial flag). Operational state per the dossier: DORMANT — the holding copy is absent, the plugin copy is unregistered in hooks.json, and LATENCY-LOG.jsonl is frozen at 10 rows (all 2026-04-20); waves W2+ never completed. Redo recipe: port the taxonomy, formulas, invariants, row schema, Iron Rule, and anti-pattern table verbatim ("the measured-universe IP... implementation-independent"); redesign the collector to emit latency rows from Native's own engine events into the ADR-013 fsync-JSONL telemetry sink "so measurement cannot silently decouple from execution"; wire D21's speed_weight into the depth/estimation flow as a real field. Gap vs Native: only scattered point latency targets exist (B5 replay ≤30s, pulse gen ≤60s, CX-bar ≤2min) plus D.11 per-tier targets and the D21 doctrine row; HLD/07 Non-Functional fill remains a TODO (T-G8-08 — "perf · security · observability · accuracy · reliability · cost · resilience").

mechanisms.title: ADR-005 host-LLM host selection — the per-workflow host decision named by matrix gap #2
mechanisms.body: ADR-005 (Accepted 2026-05-07) decides: "Native engine MUST require WorkflowStep.host ∈ {claude, codex} whenever action='invoke_host_llm'." host='claude' invokes claude --bare — recursion-safe, default for steps that must execute in the founder's session via the effector split (ADR-004); host='codex' invokes codex exec — read-only sandbox, default for analysis, review, planning steps that produce JSON/text output without state change. Per-step timeout_ms flows into host activity args; host-class default is 60s for claude --bare, ≥300s for codex. The tradeoff is locked to these two hosts in v1.x; the LLMSubstrate adapter for OpenAI/Gemini swap is deferred to the v1.x backlog. The matrix's gap #2 names this ADR — "ADR-005 selects the host-LLM per workflow" — when asking "which block issues B1's intent-parse LLM call?"
